definition_zh: 扶壁；支撑物；支持（论点、主张等）
definition_en: a structure built against a wall to support it; as a verb, to support or strengthen an argument or system
core_image: 教堂外墙斜斜伸出的石臂，稳稳抵住高墙
scene: 哥特教堂外墙边，石臂一根根斜抵着高墙。 Flying buttresses support the cathedral's towering wall.
sceneCN: 这里 buttress 是「扶壁、支撑结构」（第 1 个义项：抵住墙体的支撑构件）；句意为飞扶壁支撑着大教堂的高墙。

pos.zh: 扶壁；支撑物；支柱
支撑；加固；为（论点）提供支持

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词转形容词，义为「有扶壁支撑的；有据可依的」
由动词加 -ing 转名词，义为「支撑作用；扶壁修建」

senses.title: A structure supporting a wall
senses.definition: a projecting structure of stone or brick built against a wall to strengthen it
senses.definitionCN: 砌在墙外侧、用来加固墙体的凸出结构
senses.example: The old church leans slightly against its massive buttresses.
senses.exampleCN: 老教堂微微倚在粗大的扶壁上。
senses.why: The root means to push or strike; the buttress is the thing that pushes back against the wall.
senses.whyCN: 词根本义「推撞」，扶壁正是反向推住墙的那股力。

senses.title: Anything giving firm support
senses.definition: a person or thing that gives firm support to something, as traditions to a society
senses.definitionCN: 给某物以坚实支持的人或事物，如支撑社会的传统
senses.example: Rural custom was a buttress of the old order.
senses.exampleCN: 乡村习俗是旧秩序的一根支柱。
senses.why: The mason's prop becomes a metaphor for any load-bearing element.
senses.whyCN: 石匠的支撑物被借作任何承重因素的比喻。

senses.title: To support or strengthen (verb)
senses.definition: to make stronger by adding support, literally or figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 以支撑加固，实际或比喻义均可
senses.example: New evidence buttressed the scientist's claim.
senses.exampleCN: 新证据为这位科学家的主张提供了支撑。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb: to act as a buttress for something.
senses.whyCN: 名词转动词：为某物充当扶壁。

intro.en: Buttress grew from the same Germanic pushing root as butt, through Old French bouterez.
intro.cn: buttress 与 butt 同出日耳曼「推撞」词根，经古法语 bouterez 而来。

items.en: a root meaning to strike or push entered Old French as boter.
items.cn: 表示「击打、推撞」的日耳曼词根进入古法语 boter。

items.en: bouterez or ars bouterez named a pushing support, literally a thrusting stone.
items.cn: 古法语 bouterez（ars bouterez，「推击之术」）指以推力支撑的构件。

items.en: buttress entered English with Gothic architecture.
items.cn: 十四世纪 buttress 随哥特式建筑进入英语。

items.en: the verb sense of supporting arguments appeared in learned prose.
items.cn: 十六世纪「支撑论点」的动词义见于书面语。

items.en: flying buttress is the famous Gothic form; the figurative use is now the more common one.
items.cn: 飞扶壁是哥特建筑的名件；如今比喻用法更为常用。

examples.en: The report was buttressed by decades of field data.

definition_zh: 量子；能量或物质的最小不连续单位；定量；份额
definition_en: the smallest discrete amount of a physical quantity, or a fixed share of something
core_image: 水管里流出的水看起来连续，换成极小的量杯量，却总是一格一格地落下
scene: 炉壁烧到发红时，放出的能量并非连续不断。 Planck found that energy leaves a hot body in one quantum at a time.
sceneCN: 这里 quantum 指「能量不可再分的最小一份」（第 1 个义项：某个物理量的最小不连续单位）；句意：普朗克发现能量从炽热物体离开时，一次只放出一个量子。图中可辨识物件：炉壁、分格的能量块、温度计、记录纸。

pos.zh: 量子；定量（可数，复数形式为拉丁式）
量子的（作定语，如量子力学）

derivatives.zh: 使量子化；按离散单位处理

senses.title: The smallest discrete packet of energy
senses.titleCN: 能量不可再分的最小一份
senses.definition: the least amount of energy that can be emitted, absorbed or exchanged in a single event
senses.definitionCN: 在一次事件中被放出、吸收或交换的最小能量
senses.example: A photon carries one quantum of light energy.
senses.exampleCN: 一个光子携带一份光能量子。
senses.why: Latin quantum means 'how much', and physics narrowed that question to the smallest amount that can be counted at all.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语本义是「多少」，物理学把这个问法收窄成「能被计数的最小一份」。

senses.title: One packet of light
senses.definition: a single unit of electromagnetic energy, later called a photon
senses.definitionCN: 电磁能量的单一单位，后来称为光子
senses.example: Einstein treated each light quantum as a separate particle.
senses.exampleCN: 爱因斯坦把每一份光量子当作独立的粒子。
senses.why: Light was the first quantity found to come in packets, so the general unit became the everyday name for a light packet.
senses.whyCN: 光是最早被发现按份出现的量，于是这个通用单位成了光的一份的日常称呼。

senses.title: The plural units counted in theory
senses.titleCN: 理论中计数的复数单位
senses.definition: the countable units into which a physical quantity is divided, used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 某个物理量被分成的可数单位，通常用复数
senses.example: The theory adds up the contributions of many quanta.
senses.exampleCN: 这套理论把许多量子的贡献累加起来。
senses.why: Once a thing arrives in packets, calculations count packets, so the plural became the working noun of the theory.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某物按份到来，计算就要清点份数，于是复数成了理论的常用名词。

senses.title: The adjective of the quantum world
senses.definition: used before another noun to mark a field, state or rule that belongs to quantum theory
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前，标出属于量子理论的领域、状态或规则
senses.example: Quantum theory replaced the smooth classical picture.
senses.exampleCN: 量子理论取代了平滑的经典图景。
senses.why: English routinely turns a key noun into a modifier, so quantum now labels whole fields without changing its form.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把关键名词直接当定语，因此这个词不改词形就能标记整个领域。

senses.title: An abrupt jump between atomic states
senses.titleCN: 原子状态之间的突然跳变
senses.definition: the discontinuous change of an electron from one energy level to another
senses.definitionCN: 电子从一个能级到另一个能级的不连续变化
senses.example: The electron makes a quantum jump and emits a single photon.
senses.exampleCN: 电子发生一次量子跃迁，并放出一个光子。
senses.why: Because energy levels are discrete, a change between them cannot be gradual; it is a jump of one quantum.
senses.whyCN: 能级是分立的，因此能级之间的变化不可能渐变，只能是一份量子的跳跃。

senses.title: A sudden large advance in ordinary life
senses.titleCN: 日常语境里的突然大跨越
senses.definition: a dramatic and abrupt improvement or change, usually in the phrase quantum leap
senses.definitionCN: 戏剧性且突然的改进或变化，通常用于「量子跃迁」这一短语
senses.example: The new vaccine was a quantum leap in prevention.
senses.exampleCN: 新疫苗在预防上是巨大的一步。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the smallest possible jump in physics and reverses its scale, turning it into the biggest step imaginable.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借用了物理上最小的一跳，却把尺度反过来，变成想象中最大的一步。

senses.title: The adjective of quantum computing
senses.definition: used of information technology that exploits superposition or entanglement, as in quantum computing
senses.definitionCN: 用于利用叠加或纠缠的信息技术，如量子计算
senses.example: The laboratory built a quantum processor with a hundred units.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室造出一台拥有一百个单元的量子处理器。
senses.why: The same modifier extends to any technology built on discrete quantum states, so computing joined the family.
senses.whyCN: 同一个定语扩展到任何建立在分立量子态上的技术，于是计算也加入了这个家族。

senses.title: A required share or amount
senses.definition: a fixed amount of something required or allotted, as in a quantum of evidence
senses.definitionCN: 所需或被分配的固定分量，如「一份证据」
senses.example: The claim needs a quantum of proof before it can be heard.
senses.exampleCN: 这个说法在获准陈述之前需要一定分量的证据。
senses.why: The legal and formal sense keeps the original 'how much': a case needs a measurable minimum, not a vague impression.
senses.whyCN: 法律与正式用法保留了原本的「多少」：一个案子需要可量的最低分量，而不是模糊印象。

intro.en: Quantum is a Latin neuter form meaning 'how much', adopted by physics in 1900 for the smallest indivisible amount of energy. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: quantum 是拉丁语中性形式，意为「多少」；物理学在 1900 年用它指能量不可再分的最小一份。年代均为约数。

items.en: Quantus was the interrogative and relative adjective 'how great, how much', parallel to tantus 'so great' and qualis 'of what kind'.
items.cn: quantus 是疑问与关系形容词「多大、多少」，与「这么大」和「何种」两个词平行。

items.en: The neuter singular quantum meant 'how much', and in legal and philosophical writing it named a fixed quantity or share.
items.cn: 中性单数 quantum 意为「多少」，在法律与哲学写作中指固定的量或份额。

items.en: Planck proposed that energy is exchanged in fixed packets, and he called each packet an energy quantum, keeping the Latin question word.
items.cn: 普朗克提出能量按固定小包交换，并把每一包称为能量子，沿用了这个拉丁疑问词。

items.en: Einstein extended the idea to light, speaking of light quanta; the name photon came later, but the quantum stayed.
items.cn: 爱因斯坦把这一想法扩展到光，说到光量子；光子的名字出现得更晚，量子却留了下来。

items.en: The phrase for an electron's discontinuous change passed into general speech in the twentieth century as a figure for any sudden advance.
items.cn: 描述电子不连续变化的短语在二十世纪进入日常语言，成为任何突然进步的比喻。

items.en: The exact first written uses for the figurative and computing senses are approximate; the Latin source and the physics coinage are well dated.
items.cn: 比喻义与计算义的最早书面用例年代为约数；拉丁来源与物理学造词的年代都有明确记录。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same how-much root; group two holds amount words that overlap with quantum outside physics.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「多少」词根的词；第二组是物理学之外与 quantum 重叠的数量词。

entries.definition: From Latin quantitas, built on quantus: how much there is of something, measured without the idea of a smallest packet.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语，构于「多少」之上：某物有多少，不含「最小一份」的意思。

entries.definition: From Latin quota pars 'how great a part': an allotted share, from the same family of quantity words.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语「多大的一份」：分配到的份额，同属数量词族。

entries.definition: From Latin quorum 'of whom', the opening word of a commission's formula: the minimum number of members needed, not a quantum.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语「其中之人的」，是委任套语的开头：指所需的最低人数，并非量子。

entries.definition: Of uncertain origin and no connection with quantus: a state of puzzled doubt.
entries.definitionCN: 来源不确定，与「多少」无关：指困惑两难的处境。

entries.definition: An ordinary word for a small wrapped portion; it conveys the 'arrives in portions' idea without the physics.
entries.definitionCN: 日常指一小包东西；能传达「按份到来」的意思，但不含物理含义。

entries.definition: A general word for one countable item or standard measure; quantum is a unit fixed by nature, not by convention.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指一个可数项或标准计量；量子是由自然固定而非由人约定的单位。

entries.definition: The modern name for a light quantum; every photon is a quantum, but not every quantum is a photon.
entries.definitionCN: 光量子的现代名称；每个光子都是量子，但并非每个量子都是光子。

entries.definition: A general word for how much of something exists, with no suggestion of discreteness.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指某物有多少，不含分立性的暗示。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin quantum 'how much': physics asks how much, and finds a smallest answer.
normal.cn: 拉丁语「多少」：物理学问「多少」，却找到一个最小的答案。

normal.en: The family runs quantum, quanta, quantize, quantization, quantal.
normal.cn: 同族词包括量子、量子（复数）、使量子化、量子化、分立的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: quantum of energy, light quantum, quantum leap.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：能量子、光量子、量子跃迁。

normal.en: The same root appears in quantity and quota, both about measuring how much.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在数量与配额里，都与衡量多少有关。

normal.en: Outside physics the phrase quantum leap means a huge jump, even though a real quantum jump is the smallest possible one.
normal.cn: 物理学之外，「量子跃迁」指巨大跨越，而真正的量子跃迁恰恰是最小的一跳。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase whose steps are so small that they look like a slope from far away.
abstract.cn: 想象一级级极小的台阶，远看却像一道斜坡。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp that can only be switched to fixed brightness levels, never dimmed smoothly.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯只能调到固定的几档亮度，无法平滑变暗。

abstract.en: Picture a cash machine that pays only in whole coins, never in fractions.
abstract.cn: 想象取款机只付整枚硬币，从不付零头。

examples.en: Energy is absorbed in quanta, not in a smooth stream.
examples.cn: 能量按量子被吸收，而不是连续不断地流入。

examples.en: Each quantum of light carries a fixed amount of energy.
examples.cn: 每一份光量子都携带固定的能量。

examples.en: The discovery was a quantum leap for the whole field.
examples.cn: 这一发现对整个领域是巨大的一步。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「quant（量）+ um」——量到不能再分的那一格，就是量子

root: 拉丁 quantum「多少」，为 quantus「多大」的中性形式；同族含 quantity、quota。英语 quantum。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the smallest packet of energy, pass through the light packet, the plural units and the attributive label, then to an electron's jump, its figurative reversal, quantum computing and finally a required share.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从最小的一份能量开始，经过光的一份、复数的单位与定语用法，再到电子的一跳、被反过来用的比喻、量子计算，最后是必需的份额。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a quantity that looks continuous from afar but arrives in indivisible steps when measured closely.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个远看连续的量，凑近测量时却按不可分的台阶到来。

branches.en: THE PACKET: energy and light are the same discovery seen twice, since light was the first quantity found in packets.
branches.cn: 小包：能量与光是同一发现的两面，因为光是最早被发现按包出现的量。

branches.en: THE COUNT: once things arrive in packets, theory counts packets and the plural becomes a working noun.
branches.cn: 计数：一旦事物按包到来，理论就清点包数，复数便成了常用名词。

branches.en: THE LABEL: the noun turns into a modifier and marks whole fields, from theory to computing.
branches.cn: 标签：名词转成定语，标记整个领域，从理论到计算。

branches.en: THE JUMP: discreteness forces an abrupt change, and everyday speech borrows it while reversing its size.
branches.cn: 跳跃：分立性迫使变化突然发生，日常语言借走它，却把大小反过来。

branches.en: THE SHARE: law and formal prose keep the original question and ask for a measurable minimum.
branches.cn: 份额：法律与正式文章保留原本的「多少」，要求一个可量的最低分量。

intro.en: Quantum is a Latin pronominal adjective turned noun, and its root family is small but busy in English.
intro.cn: quantum 是拉丁代词性形容词转成的名词，它的词根词族不大，却在英语里很活跃。

latinIntro.en: Latin quantus and quantum yield quantity, quantify, quantitative and quota in English; the ending -um marks the neuter form used as a noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 quantus 与 quantum 在英语里衍生出数量、量化、定量的与配额；-um 结尾标出用作名词的中性形式。

items.example: The adjective asks for a measure of size.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词问的是大小或分量。

items.example: The ending turns the adjective into an abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾把形容词变成抽象名词。

items.structure: quantum (neuter of quantus, used as a noun)
items.example: The court asked for a quantum of proof.
items.exampleCN: 法庭要求一定分量的证据。

items.example: The theory sums over many quanta.
items.exampleCN: 理论对许多量子求和。

items.example: Engineers quantize the signal before storing it.
items.exampleCN: 工程师在存储前先把信号量化。

definition_zh: 后代；子女；子孙；（事物的）产物、成果
definition_en: the young or offspring of a person, animal or plant, or the product that something brings forth
core_image: 一株母本植物在温室内分出整齐的幼苗行列，每一行都接着上一代的性状
scene: 温室里，育种者把同一母株的后代逐代排开，记录性状如何分离。 Seedlings raised from a single parent plant form one visible progeny.
sceneCN: 这里 progeny 指「同一亲本繁育出的后代群体」（第 1 个义项：人或动植物的后代）；句意为温室里由单一母株育出的幼苗排成一行行，构成一个可见的后代群体。可辨识物件：育苗盘、幼苗、手写标签、温室玻璃。

pos.zh: 后代；子女；子孙（集合名词）

senses.title: Offspring of a living thing
senses.definition: the young produced by a person, animal or plant
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物繁育出的幼体
senses.example: The mare's progeny all inherited her calm temperament.
senses.exampleCN: 这匹母马的后代都继承了她沉静的性情。
senses.why: Progeny is a mass noun for what is brought forth, so it treats the young as a collective result rather than counting them one by one.
senses.whyCN: progeny 是把「被生出来之物」当作整体的集合名词，因此把幼体视作一个总的结果，而不是逐个计数。

senses.title: A line of descendants
senses.definition: the whole line of descendants from an ancestor
senses.definitionCN: 从某一祖先延续下来的整条世系
senses.example: The estate passed through his progeny for four generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这座庄园在他的子孙中传了四代。
senses.why: The Latin noun named a line of descent, so English progeny can mean the whole chain, not only the immediate young.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词本指一条世系，因此英语 progeny 可以指整条链，而不只是眼前的幼体。

senses.title: Offspring of a plant
senses.definition: the seedlings or bulbs produced by a parent plant
senses.definitionCN: 由母株繁育出的幼苗或球茎
senses.example: Gardeners sell the progeny of that famous rose.
senses.exampleCN: 园艺师出售那株名贵月季的子代。
senses.why: Because plants also beget, the word applies to seedlings and bulbs without any change of form.
senses.whyCN: 植物同样会繁育，因此这个词不加任何词形变化就可用于幼苗与球茎。

senses.title: A product of a cause
senses.definition: something produced as a result of another thing or process
senses.definitionCN: 由另一事物或过程产生的结果
senses.example: The theory is the progeny of two older debates.
senses.exampleCN: 这套理论是两场更早争论的产物。
senses.why: The metaphor treats an idea as a child: what comes forth from a cause is its progeny.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻把观念当作孩子：从原因中产出的东西就是它的后代。

senses.title: Successors or followers
senses.definition: the people who continue a tradition or institution
senses.definitionCN: 延续某一传统或机构的人
senses.example: The movement's progeny now run several publishing houses.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动的后来者如今经营着几家出版社。
senses.why: People who continue a tradition are pictured as its descendants, so the word covers institutional heirs.
senses.whyCN: 延续传统的人被想象成它的子孙，因此这个词也涵盖机构意义上的继承者。

senses.title: Progeny testing in breeding
senses.definition: the practice of judging a parent by the performance of its offspring
senses.definitionCN: 以后代的表现来评判亲本优劣的做法
senses.example: Progeny testing decides which bull is kept for breeding.
senses.exampleCN: 后代测验决定哪头公牛留作种用。
senses.why: In animal breeding the word is fixed in the phrase progeny testing, where the offspring's performance is the evidence.
senses.whyCN: 在畜牧育种中，这个词固定于 progeny testing 这一短语，以子代的表现作为证据。

senses.title: A group taken collectively
senses.titleCN: 作为一个整体看待的后代群
senses.definition: the offspring of one parent considered as a single group
senses.definitionCN: 把同一亲本的后代视作一个整体
senses.example: The whole progeny was raised in the same nursery.
senses.exampleCN: 整批后代都在同一间育苗室中育成。
senses.why: The noun often takes a singular verb because it names a group; this collective reading is why a plural in -ies is unusual.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词常接单数动词，因为它命名的是一个群体；这种集合用法正是它少用 -ies 复数的原因。

senses.title: A legacy carried forward
senses.titleCN: 延续下来的遗产（作品、影响）
senses.definition: the lasting work or influence that survives its source
senses.definitionCN: 在源头之后仍然存续的作品或影响
senses.example: Her progeny is a school of composers who still use her method.
senses.exampleCN: 她留下的传承是一批至今仍用她方法的作曲家。
senses.why: The figurative sense can outlast biology: what survives is not a child but a body of work.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义可以超出生物学：存续下来的不是孩子，而是一整套作品。

intro.en: Progeny came into English through Old French from Latin progenies 'line of descent, offspring', a derivative of progignere 'bring forth', itself pro- 'forth' plus gignere 'beget'.
intro.cn: progeny 经古法语进入英语，源自拉丁 progenies「世系、后代」，由 progignere「向前生出」派生，而后者是 pro-「向前」加 gignere「生育」。

items.en: Gignere 'to beget, bring forth' is the source of genitor and generate. Its pre-Latin form is reconstructed as PIE *ǵenh₁-, so the starred form is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: gignere「生育、产生」是 genitor 与 generate 的来源。它在拉丁语之前的形式被重构为原始印欧语 *ǵenh₁-，带星号的形式属于重构形式，并非有记录的词。

items.en: Pro- 'forth' plus gignere produced progignere 'bring forth'; its noun progenies named the line of descent rather than a single child.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 gignere 构成 progignere「向前生出」；其名词 progenies 指一条世系，而非单个孩子。

items.en: Old French progenie carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century; the exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 古法语 progenie 在 14 世纪把这个名词带入英语；确切的最早书证年代不确定。

items.en: By the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries progeny was applied to works, results and successors, not only living offspring.
items.cn: 到 16、17 世纪，progeny 已被用于作品、结果与后继者，不再仅指活着的后代。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the internal structure of the PIE root is reconstructed, and competing reconstructions exist, so no single form should be treated as settled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：该原始印欧词根的内部结构属于重构，且存在互相竞争的多种重构，因此不应把任何单一形式当作定论。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like progeny or share its root; group two holds the ordinary words for offspring and descendants.
note.cn: 第一组是与 progeny 形近或同根的词；第二组是表示后代与子孙的常用近义词。

entries.tag: same root the one who begets
entries.definition: The agent noun from the same Latin stem: a forefather or precursor, not the offspring itself.

entries.definition: An adjective built on the Latin stem, meaning capable of producing offspring; it describes a capacity, not the young.

entries.definition: A rare noun for the act of bringing forth or the offspring produced; it survives mostly in older legal and literary writing.

entries.definition: From Latin prodigium 'portent', not from gignere: a marvel or a child of exceptional talent. The resemblance is only in sound.

entries.definition: The everyday term for the young of a person or animal; it counts individuals more readily than progeny.
entries.definitionCN: 指人或动物幼体的日常通称；比 progeny 更容易逐个计数。

entries.definition: A person or group descended from an ancestor, often used for distant generations rather than the immediate young.
entries.definitionCN: 指某一祖先传下的人或群体，常用于较远的世代而非眼前的幼体。

entries.definition: In law and formal writing, issue means offspring or descendants, especially in wills and genealogies.
entries.definitionCN: 在法律与正式文体中，issue 指后代或子嗣，尤见于遗嘱与族谱。

entries.definition: The whole set of young hatched or born at one time, usually birds; it stresses the group, not the lineage.
entries.definitionCN: 指一次孵化或出生的一整窝幼体，多用于鸟类；强调群体而非世系。

dict_mnemonic.text: pro（向前）+ gen（生）——向前生出来的一群 → 后代；注意别与 prodigy（奇才、预兆）混。

root: 拉丁 progenies「世系、后代」← pro-（向前）+ gignere（生育）；gignere 与 generate、gene 同出原始印欧语 *ǵenh₁-（重构形式），更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: something is brought forth, and that bringing-forth is then read as offspring, lineage, plant young, a product, successors, a breeding test, a collective group and finally a surviving body of work.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：某物被生出，这一「生出」随后被读作后代、世系、植物子代、产物、后继者、育种测验、集合群体，最后是存续下来的作品整体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a parent plant sending up a row of seedlings, each carrying part of the same pattern.

branches.en: LIVING OFFSPRING: animals and plants both bring forth young, and the noun covers either.
branches.cn: 活着的后代：动物与植物都会繁育幼体，这个词两者都覆盖。

branches.en: LINE AND GROUP: the same noun names a chain of generations or one parent's whole brood.
branches.cn: 世系与群体：同一个名词既指代代相连的链，也指某一亲本的整批子代。

branches.en: PRODUCT: an idea or result is pictured as what a cause gives birth to.
branches.cn: 产物：观念或结果被想象成原因所生之物。

branches.en: SUCCESSORS AND WORK: people who carry on a tradition, and the work that outlives its maker.
branches.cn: 后继者与作品：延续传统的人，以及比作者活得更久的作品。

branches.en: BREEDING TEST: the offspring's performance becomes the evidence for judging the parent.
branches.cn: 育种测验：子代表现成为评判亲本的证据。

intro.en: Progeny is a Latin noun whose prefix and root also build several English words, so the family can be read morpheme by morpheme.

senses.example: A clear quartz crystal glittered among the river pebbles.
senses.exampleCN: 一颗透明石英晶体在河卵石间闪光。
senses.why: Quartz is defined by its composition and lattice, not by colour or shape; those vary while the mineral stays the same.
senses.whyCN: 石英由成分与晶格定义，而非颜色或形状；后者会变，矿物本身不变。

senses.title: A crystal with six-sided prisms
senses.definition: a quartz crystal showing hexagonal prisms and pointed terminations
senses.definitionCN: 呈六棱柱与尖顶形态的石英晶体
senses.example: The quartz grew as a six-sided prism in the cavity.
senses.exampleCN: 石英在晶洞中长成六棱柱。
senses.why: Its lattice repeats in six-fold symmetry, so a freely grown crystal takes a hexagonal outline.
senses.whyCN: 其晶格以六重对称重复，因此自由生长的晶体呈六边形轮廓。

senses.title: The main component of sand
senses.definition: quartz grains that survive weathering and make up most sand and sandstone
senses.definitionCN: 经风化残留、构成大部分砂与砂岩的石英颗粒
senses.example: Most beach sand is quartz that rivers carried to the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 多数海滩砂是河流带到海边的石英。
senses.why: Quartz resists chemical weathering, so it outlasts other minerals and accumulates as sand.
senses.whyCN: 石英抗化学风化，因此比其它矿物存留更久，堆积成砂。

senses.title: A piezoelectric material
senses.definition: quartz used in watches, radios, and sensors because it generates charge when squeezed
senses.definitionCN: 因受压产生电荷而用于钟表、无线电与传感器的石英
senses.example: The quartz in the watch vibrates at a precise frequency.
senses.exampleCN: 手表中的石英以精确频率振动。
senses.why: Its regular lattice converts mechanical stress into electrical signal, which is why clocks can count it.
senses.whyCN: 其规整晶格把机械应力转为电信号，因此钟表可以「数」它。

senses.title: A gem and ornamental stone
senses.definition: clear or coloured quartz varieties valued as gems and carvings
senses.definitionCN: 作为宝石与雕刻材料而受珍视的透明或彩色石英变种
senses.example: Rose quartz is carved into small figures.
senses.exampleCN: 粉晶被雕成小摆件。
senses.why: Impurities add colour while the hard lattice takes a polish, turning a common mineral into a gem.
senses.whyCN: 杂质带来颜色，坚硬晶格又能抛光，于是常见矿物变成宝石。

senses.title: A vein in hydrothermal deposits
senses.definition: quartz filling cracks where hot mineral-rich water deposited silica
senses.definitionCN: 富含矿物的热水沉淀二氧化硅、充填裂缝形成的石英
senses.example: Gold often sits in quartz veins.
senses.exampleCN: 黄金常赋存于石英脉中。
senses.why: Hot fluids carry silica and metals together; when they cool, quartz seals the crack and traps the ore.
senses.whyCN: 热液同时携带硅与金属；冷却时石英封住裂缝并圈闭矿石。

senses.title: A dust hazard
senses.definition: fine quartz dust that damages lungs when inhaled over years
senses.definitionCN: 长期吸入会损伤肺部的细石英粉尘
senses.example: Cutting stone without water raises quartz dust.
senses.exampleCN: 无水切割石材会产生石英粉尘。
senses.why: Hardness makes the mineral useful, and the same hardness makes its dust cut lung tissue.
senses.whyCN: 硬度使矿物有用，同样的硬度又使粉尘割伤肺组织。

senses.title: An industrial raw material
senses.definition: quartz sand and crushed quartz used in glass, ceramics, and foundry moulds
senses.definitionCN: 用于玻璃、陶瓷与铸造砂型的石英砂与碎石英
senses.example: The glassworks buys pure quartz sand by the tonne.
senses.exampleCN: 玻璃厂成吨购买纯石英砂。
senses.why: Silica is the backbone of glass, so a cheap, pure source of quartz is an industrial necessity.
senses.whyCN: 二氧化硅是玻璃的骨架，因此廉价纯净的石英来源是工业必需品。

senses.title: Abstract: clear, hard, and unchanging
senses.definition: a quality of transparency combined with stubborn constancy
senses.definitionCN: 透明与固执恒常相结合的性质
senses.example: Her quartz clarity hid a very hard will.
senses.exampleCN: 她水晶般的清澈之下藏着极硬的意志。
senses.why: The metaphor joins two properties of the mineral: you can see through it, yet it yields to almost nothing.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻结合矿物的两种属性：看得透，却几乎不为外物所动。

intro.en: Quartz entered English from German in the sixteenth century, probably from a Slavic word for hard. The deeper origin is uncertain. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: quartz 在 16 世纪从德语进入英语，可能来自斯拉夫语中表示「坚硬」的词。更深来源不确定。年代均为约数。

items.en: German miners called the mineral Quarz; Middle High German forms include twarc and quarc, showing that the word was still unsettled.
items.cn: 德国矿工把这种矿物称作 Quarz；中古高地德语形式包括 twarc 与 quarc，说明词形当时尚未固定。

items.en: The German word is generally thought to come from a Slavic adjective meaning 'hard', represented by Czech tvrdy and Polish twardy.
items.cn: 一般认为这个德语词来自斯拉夫语中意为「坚硬」的形容词，如捷克语 tvrdy 与波兰语 twardy。

items.en: Source uncertain: the Slavic adjective goes back to a reconstructed Proto-Slavic form, and its earlier Indo-European history is debated.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个斯拉夫语形容词可上溯到一个重构的原始斯拉夫语形式，其更早的印欧语历史仍有争议。

items.en: English adopted quartz in the sixteenth century, when mineralogy was beginning to name substances systematically.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入 quartz，当时矿物学正开始系统地为物质命名。

items.en: Piezoelectric and optical uses developed in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, adding technical senses to the mineral name.
items.cn: 压电与光学用途在 19、20 世纪发展起来，为这一矿物名增添了技术含义。

note.en: Group one holds minerals and varieties that are chemically close to quartz; group two holds materials often confused with it.
note.cn: 第一组是化学上与石英接近的矿物与变种；第二组是常与石英混淆的材料。

entries.definition: A metamorphic rock made almost entirely of quartz grains; quartz is the mineral, quartzite the rock.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎全由石英颗粒构成的变质岩；石英是矿物，石英岩是岩石。

entries.definition: Meaning rich in quartz; it describes a rock's composition rather than naming the mineral.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「富含石英的」；它描述岩石成分，而非命名矿物。

entries.definition: Silicon dioxide as a substance, including its non-crystalline forms; quartz is its crystalline mineral form.
entries.definitionCN: 作为物质的二氧化硅，包括非晶形态；石英是它的结晶矿物形态。

entries.definition: Calcium carbonate, softer than quartz and reacting with acid; it is easily mistaken in the field.
entries.definitionCN: 碳酸钙，比石英软且遇酸反应；野外容易误认。

entries.definition: Purple quartz coloured by iron and radiation; it is quartz with a gem variety name.
entries.definitionCN: 由铁与辐射致色的紫色石英；它是带宝石变种名的石英。

entries.definition: Clear, colourless quartz; the old name distinguishes the gem form from ordinary grains.
entries.definitionCN: 透明无色的石英；这一旧名把宝石形态与普通颗粒区分开。

entries.definition: A hard, fine-grained silica rock; it is chemically like quartz but lacks visible crystals.
entries.definitionCN: 坚硬细粒的二氧化硅岩石；化学成分似石英，但无可见晶体。

entries.definition: Glass made by melting quartz; it keeps silica's properties without a crystal lattice.
entries.definitionCN: 熔融石英制成的玻璃；保留二氧化硅性质，但没有晶格。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real etymology notes, real mineral names and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实词源注记、真实矿物名称与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Quartz is silicon dioxide; hardness and acid resistance follow from that chemistry.
normal.cn: 石英是二氧化硅；硬度与耐酸性都由此化学性质而来。

normal.en: Six-sided prisms grow because the lattice repeats in six-fold symmetry.
normal.cn: 六棱柱源于晶格的六重对称重复。

normal.en: Most sand is quartz that outlasted everything else.
normal.cn: 多数砂是熬过其它矿物的石英。

normal.en: Quartz watches count the vibration of a quartz plate.
normal.cn: 石英表数的是石英片的振动。

normal.en: Quartz, quartzite, quartzose, silica, amethyst form one family.
normal.cn: quartz、quartzite、quartzose、silica、amethyst 构成一个词族。

abstract.en: Picture a window that is also a stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇同时是石头的窗。

abstract.en: Picture a tuning fork made of rock, humming at one exact pitch.
abstract.cn: 想象一把石头做的音叉，以某个精确音高嗡鸣。

abstract.en: Picture a person you can see through but cannot move.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人，你看得透，却推不动。

examples.en: A clear quartz crystal glittered among the river pebbles.
examples.cn: 一颗透明石英晶体在河卵石间闪光。

examples.en: Quartz resists weathering, so it survives as sand long after other minerals decay.
examples.cn: 石英抗风化，因此在其它矿物分解后仍以砂的形式存留。

examples.en: The vein of quartz carries tiny amounts of gold.
examples.cn: 这条石英脉含有微量黄金。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「夸兹」——透明、坚硬、能报时的石头 → 石英

root: 德语 Quarz，可能来自斯拉夫语表示「坚硬」的形容词（捷克语 tvrdy、波兰语 twardy），再上溯重构的原始斯拉夫语形式；更深印欧语来源有争议。化学成分二氧化硅。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from the mineral's composition to its crystal shape, its sand, its technical uses, its gem forms, its veins, its dust, its industry, and finally to clarity as a character image.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从矿物成分走到晶体形态、砂粒、技术用途、宝石形态、矿脉、粉尘、工业，最后落到作为性格意象的清澈。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a transparent six-sided crystal catching light among ordinary river pebbles.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗透明六棱晶体在普通河卵石之间反光。

branches.en: COMPOSITION AND FORM: the same silica lattice explains both the mineral's identity and its six-sided shape.
branches.cn: 成分与形态：同一二氧化硅晶格既解释矿物身份，也解释六棱外形。

branches.en: SURVIVOR: hardness and acid resistance let quartz outlast other minerals as sand.
branches.cn: 幸存者：硬度与耐酸性让石英以砂的形式熬过其它矿物。

branches.en: SIGNAL AND VEIN: the lattice converts stress into charge, and hot fluids deposit quartz in cracks.
branches.cn: 信号与矿脉：晶格把应力转为电荷，热液则在裂缝中沉淀石英。

branches.en: BEAUTY AND USE: impurities make gems, while cheap pure grains make glass and moulds.
branches.cn: 美与用：杂质造宝石，廉价纯净颗粒则造玻璃与砂型。

branches.en: HARDNESS TWO WAYS: dust cuts lungs, and the same unyielding clarity becomes a human metaphor.
branches.cn: 坚硬的两种方向：粉尘割肺，同样的不屈清澈又成为人的比喻。

intro.en: Quartz has a small but clear family of mineral and technical derivatives.
intro.cn: quartz 的词族不大，但矿物与技术派生词脉络清楚。

latinIntro.en: Quartz is not Latin in origin; the related technical vocabulary uses Latin silica and Greek krystallos.
latinIntro.cn: quartz 并非拉丁语来源；相关技术词汇使用拉丁语 silica 与希腊语 krystallos。

items.structure: German Quarz, from Middle High German twarc
items.example: German miners spread the name Quarz.
items.exampleCN: 德国矿工传播了 Quarz 这个名称。

items.example: Quartz is hard and resists acid.
items.exampleCN: 石英坚硬且耐酸。

items.example: The quartzose sandstone is very hard.
items.exampleCN: 这块石英质砂岩非常坚硬。

items.example: Quartzite forms when sandstone recrystallizes.
items.exampleCN: 砂岩重结晶时形成石英岩。

items.example: A quartziferous vein cuts the limestone.
items.exampleCN: 一条含石英矿脉切穿石灰岩。

items.example: Silica is the chemical backbone of quartz.
items.exampleCN: 二氧化硅是石英的化学骨架。

items.example: Amethyst is quartz with iron colouring.
items.exampleCN: 紫水晶是含铁致色的石英。

items.structure: origin uncertain, perhaps from flint terminology
items.meaningCN: 隐晶质二氧化硅岩石；燧石类
items.example: Chert has the chemistry of quartz without visible crystals.
items.exampleCN: 燧石具石英的化学性质，却无可见晶体。

items.meaning: a solid with a regular lattice
items.meaningCN: 具规则晶格的固体；晶体
items.example: A quartz crystal has six-fold symmetry.
items.exampleCN: 石英晶体具六重对称。

latinEntries.structure: Greek krystallos (ice, crystal), borrowed into Latin

definition_zh: 认知的；与知觉、记忆、推理等思维过程有关的
definition_en: relating to the mental processes of perceiving, remembering, reasoning and knowing
core_image: 一张脑内地图上标着看、记、想三个相连的节点
scene: 老师让学生先记住一串数字，再做一道逻辑题，比较两种任务的表现。 The teacher asks students to memorize a string of digits and then solve a logic puzzle, comparing their performance on two cognitive tasks.
sceneCN: 这里 cognitive 指「与思维过程有关的」（第 1 个义项：知觉、记忆、推理这类活动）；句意为老师让学生记数字再做逻辑题，比较两种认知任务的表现。图中可辨识物件：数字串、逻辑题、两块答题板、计时器。

pos.zh: 认知的；与思维过程有关的

derivatives.zh: 元认知的（对自己的思考进行思考）

senses.title: Relating to thinking processes
senses.definition: concerning perception, memory, reasoning or other mental processes
senses.definitionCN: 关乎知觉、记忆、推理或其他心理过程
senses.example: The teacher compares performance on two cognitive tasks.
senses.exampleCN: 老师比较两项认知任务的表现。
senses.why: the adjective adds -ive 'tending to' to the noun stem, so it describes anything that belongs to the business of knowing.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词在名词词干后加 -ive「倾向于」，描述一切属于「认识」这件事的东西。

senses.title: Of cognitive psychology
senses.definition: belonging to the branch of psychology that studies mental processes
senses.definitionCN: 属于研究心理过程的心理学分支
senses.example: The lab runs a cognitive psychology experiment on attention.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室做了一项关于注意的认知心理学实验。
senses.why: a discipline needs an adjective for its own subject matter, and this word supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 一门学科需要为本学科的研究对象配一个形容词，这个词正好补上。

senses.title: Cognitive development
senses.definition: the growth of perception, memory and reasoning from infancy onward
senses.definitionCN: 从婴儿期起知觉、记忆与推理的发展
senses.example: Picture books support cognitive development in toddlers.
senses.exampleCN: 图画书有助于幼儿的认知发展。
senses.why: development adds time to cognition; the adjective marks which line of growth is being measured.
senses.whyCN: 发展给认知加上时间；这个形容词标明被测量的是哪一条成长线。

senses.title: Cognitive bias and cognitive load
senses.definition: used in fixed terms for systematic errors of judgment and for the mental effort a task demands
senses.definitionCN: 用于固定术语，指判断的系统性偏差以及任务所需的心智努力
senses.example: Long instructions raise cognitive load before the task begins.
senses.exampleCN: 冗长的说明在任务开始前就提高了认知负荷。
senses.why: once a field finds regular failure modes, it names them with the same adjective: bias in judging, load in working memory.
senses.whyCN: 一个领域发现规律性的失败模式后，就用同一个形容词命名它们：判断中的偏差、工作记忆中的负荷。

senses.title: Cognitive linguistics
senses.definition: relating to the approach that treats language as shaped by general mental processes
senses.definitionCN: 属于把语言视为一般心智过程之产物的研究取向
senses.example: Cognitive linguistics treats metaphor as ordinary thought.
senses.exampleCN: 认知语言学把隐喻视为日常思维。
senses.why: the adjective lets a whole school declare its base: language is not a separate module but part of cognition.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词让整个学派声明自己的立足点：语言不是独立模块，而是认知的一部分。

senses.title: Cognitive therapy
senses.definition: relating to treatment that works on thought patterns rather than only on behavior
senses.definitionCN: 属于针对思维模式而非只针对行为的治疗
senses.example: Cognitive therapy asks the patient to test a fearful belief.
senses.exampleCN: 认知疗法要求病人检验一个恐惧信念。
senses.why: if distorted thinking maintains distress, then changing the thinking is a route to changing the distress.
senses.whyCN: 如果扭曲的思维维持着痛苦，那么改变思维就是改变痛苦的一条路径。

senses.title: Belonging to cognitive science
senses.definition: relating to the interdisciplinary study of mind, information and computation
senses.definitionCN: 属于心智、信息与计算的交叉研究
senses.example: The programme combines cognitive and computational methods.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目结合认知方法与计算方法。
senses.why: the adjective becomes a badge of a field that borrows from psychology, linguistics, neuroscience and computing at once.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词成了一个领域的徽章，它同时借用心理学、语言学、神经科学与计算。

senses.title: Cognitive meaning in language
senses.definition: the conceptual content a word carries, as opposed to its emotional colouring
senses.definitionCN: 词语承载的概念内容，与情感色彩相对
senses.example: The cognitive meaning of home is a dwelling, not a feeling.
senses.exampleCN: 「家」这个词的认知意义是住所，而不是一种情感。
senses.why: linguists split meaning into what it denotes and what it evokes; the adjective labels the denotative half.
senses.whyCN: 语言学家把意义分为「指什么」与「唤起什么」；这个形容词标记前者。

intro.en: Cognitive is Medieval Latin cognitivus, built on the participle stem of cognoscere 'to get to know' plus -ivus. It entered English in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cognitive 是晚期拉丁 cognitivus，由 cognoscere「得知」的分词词干加 -ivus 构成。它在 16 世纪进入英语。年代为约数。

items.en: Cognoscere 'to get to know' joins com- 'thoroughly' to gnoscere 'to know'; its participle stem is cognit-.
items.cn: cognoscere「得知」把 com-「彻底」与 gnoscere「知道」结合；其分词词干为 cognit-。

items.en: Scholastic Latin formed cognitivus 'having the power of knowing' from cognit- plus the adjective suffix -ivus.
items.cn: 经院拉丁语由 cognit- 加形容词后缀 -ivus 构成 cognitivus，意为「具有认识能力的」。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the sixteenth century, at first in philosophical writing about the powers of the mind.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入这个形容词，最初用于讨论心智能力的哲学著作。

items.en: Cognitive psychology, cognitive science and cognitive therapy all took their names in the twentieth century, when the mind was studied as an information processor.
items.cn: 认知心理学、认知科学与认知疗法都在 20 世纪得名，当时心智被当作信息加工系统来研究。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest English citation is not precisely fixed, and the medieval coinage may have been influenced by Greek-derived models in scholastic Latin.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：最早的英语书证没有精确年代；这一中世纪新造词可能受经院拉丁语中希腊式构词模式的影响。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same knowing stem; group two holds adjectives about mental life with different scope.
note.cn: 第一组是同一「知」词干的形式；第二组是范围不同的心智形容词。

entries.definition: The processes themselves; cognitive is the adjective that describes them or the tasks that measure them.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程本身；cognitive 是描述这些过程或测量任务的形容词。

entries.definition: Knowing that something is the case; it means 'aware of', not 'relating to thinking processes'.
entries.definitionCN: 知道某事属实；意为「知晓」，不是「与思维过程有关」。

entries.definition: Relating to serious thought and learning; it comes from intellectus, another descendant of the same legere family.
entries.definitionCN: 与严肃思考及学识有关的；来自 intellectus，是同一 legere 词族的另一支。

entries.definition: Related by descent in language; its second element is gnatus 'born', so it is not about thinking.
entries.definitionCN: 语言上同源的；第二部分是 gnatus「出生」，与思维无关。

entries.definition: Relating to the mind in general, including emotion and will; cognitive is narrower and points to knowing.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指心智，包括情绪与意志；cognitive 更窄，指向「知」。

entries.definition: Relating to the senses and to what is taken in; perception is only the first stage of cognition.
entries.definitionCN: 与感官及所接收之物有关；知觉只是认知的第一阶段。

entries.definition: Following reason and logic; rational judges the quality of thinking, while cognitive only locates its domain.
entries.definitionCN: 遵循理性与逻辑；rational 评判思考的质量，cognitive 只标出所属领域。

entries.definition: Relating to psychology, including emotion, motivation and social behavior; cognitive covers only the knowing side.
entries.definitionCN: 与心理学有关，包含情绪、动机与社会行为；cognitive 只覆盖「知」的一面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: cognit- 'know' + -ive 'tending to': anything that belongs to the work of knowing.
normal.cn: cognit-「知」+ -ive「倾向于」：一切属于「认识」这件事的东西。

normal.en: The family runs cognition, cognitive, cognitively, cognitivism and metacognitive.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 cognition、cognitive、cognitively、cognitivism 与 metacognitive。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: cognitive development, cognitive science, cognitive bias, cognitive load.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：认知发展、认知科学、认知偏差、认知负荷。

normal.en: Cognitive describes the domain, not the quality; a cognitive bias can be irrational.
normal.cn: cognitive 描述领域，而非质量；认知偏差可以是不理性的。

normal.en: The adverb cognitively usually modifies verbs such as process, assess or decline.
normal.cn: 副词形式通常修饰「加工、评估、衰退」这类动词。

abstract.en: Picture a map with three marked stops: see, store, infer.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图标出三站：看、存、推。

abstract.en: Picture a workbench where raw sensory material is turned into a finished judgment.
abstract.cn: 想象一张工作台，把感官原料加工成判断成品。

abstract.en: Picture a light that falls only on the thinking half of a face.
abstract.cn: 想象一束光只照在脸孔中「思考」的那一半。

examples.en: Cognitive development is fastest in the first years of life.
examples.cn: 认知发展在生命最初几年最快。

examples.en: The test measures cognitive flexibility rather than factual recall.
examples.cn: 这项测验衡量认知灵活性，而非事实记忆。

examples.en: Cognitive therapy helped her question the belief that she was failing.
examples.cn: 认知疗法帮助她质疑自己正在失败这一信念。

dict_mnemonic.text: cognition（认知）+ ive（……的）——属于认知活动的 → 认知的

root: 晚期拉丁 cognitivus「有认识能力的」← cognit-（cognoscere「得知」的分词词干）+ -ivus；与 cognition 同族。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses show the adjective attaching itself to tasks, to a discipline, to development, to named failure modes, to a school, to a therapy, to a field and to a slice of meaning.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项显示这个形容词依次贴到任务、学科、发展、有名的失败模式、学派、疗法、领域，以及意义的一个切面上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tag marked 'knowing' pinned onto one item after another.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚写着「知」的标签，被钉到一个又一个事物上。

branches.en: THE DOMAIN: the adjective first marks the mental territory and the discipline that owns it.
branches.cn: 领域：这个形容词先标出心智领地，以及拥有这片领地的学科。

branches.en: TIME: development adds a growing line to the same territory.
branches.cn: 时间：发展给同一片领地加上一条生长的线。

branches.en: FAILURE MODES: bias and load are the named ways the machinery strains.
branches.cn: 失败模式：偏差与负荷是这台机器吃力时被命名的样子。

branches.en: APPLICATIONS: a linguistic school and a therapy both claim the adjective as their base.
branches.cn: 应用：一个语言学派与一种疗法都把这个形容词当作自己的根基。

branches.en: INSTITUTION AND MEANING: the adjective labels an interdisciplinary field and the denotative half of a word.
branches.cn: 建制与意义：这个形容词既标出一个交叉学科，也标出词语意义中「指物」的一半。

intro.en: Cognitive is a Latin participle stem plus the adjective suffix -ive; it has no independent prefix of its own, since com- is already inside the stem.
intro.cn: cognitive 是拉丁分词词干加形容词后缀 -ive；它本身没有独立前缀，因为 com- 已经含在词干里。

latinIntro.en: Cognoscere 'to get to know' yields cognit- and cognitivus; English adds cognition, cognitive, cognitively and the modern compound metacognitive.
latinIntro.cn: cognoscere「得知」生成 cognit- 与 cognitivus；英语再加上 cognition、cognitive、cognitively 与现代复合词 metacognitive。

items.example: The stem carries the finished act of knowing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干承载已完成的「知」。

items.meaning: tending to, having the nature of
items.example: The suffix turns the stem into a descriptive adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把词干变成描述性形容词。

items.example: Cognitive tasks test more than memory.
items.exampleCN: 认知任务测验的不止记忆。

items.meaning: the act or faculty of knowing
items.example: Cognition is the noun behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: cognition 是形容词背后的名词。

items.example: The patient remained cognitively intact.
items.exampleCN: 病人在认知上保持完好。

items.meaning: the view that mind is information processing
items.meaningCN: 认为心智是信息加工的观点
items.example: Cognitivism dominated psychology in the 1970s.
items.exampleCN: 认知主义在 20 世纪 70 年代主导心理学。

items.example: A cognitivist treats beliefs as representations.
items.exampleCN: 认知主义者把信念当作表征。

items.meaning: relating to thinking about one's own thinking
items.meaningCN: 元认知的；对自己的思考进行思考的
items.example: Metacognitive strategies help students monitor themselves.
items.exampleCN: 元认知策略帮助学生监控自己。

items.example: Cognoscere is the ultimate source of the family.
items.exampleCN: cognoscere 是整个词族的最终来源。

definition_zh: 在远处；远离家乡；在野外；在战场上
definition_en: at a distance from home or from the usual place, especially in far afield; in older use, out in open country or on campaign
core_image: 离开自家那块地，走到外面的田野去
scene: 这家小厂原本只卖给邻镇，如今客户远及海外。 The firm now sells far afield.
sceneCN: 这里 afield 是「在远处」（第 1 个义项：远离本地、到远方去）；句意为这家厂如今把货卖到很远的地方。核心画面是离开自家那块地，走到外面的田野去。

pos.zh: 在远处；远离家乡；在野外

forms.label: 无比较级与最高级（副词，常与 far 或 further 连用）

derivatives.zh: 去掉前缀 a- 的名词，义为「田地；场地；领域」
field 加 work 构成，义为「实地考察；田野工作」
out 加 field 构成，义为「外场；外围地带」

senses.title: Far from home or the usual place
senses.definition: at a distance from the place where you live or normally work, especially in the phrase far afield
senses.definitionCN: 离你居住或平常工作的地方有一段距离，尤用于 far afield 这一短语
senses.example: Collectors come from far afield to see the collection.
senses.exampleCN: 收藏爱好者从很远的地方赶来看这批藏品。
senses.why: The prefix a- here means on or in, so afield is literally in the field: once you leave your own plot you are out in open country, which is far from home.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 a- 表示「在……上／中」，所以 afield 字面是「在田地里」：一旦离开自家那块地，你就到了外面的旷野，也就是离家很远的地方。

senses.title: Out on open ground or on campaign
senses.definition: out in the open country, or away on a military campaign, the older literal sense of the word
senses.definitionCN: 在外面的旷野中，或出征在外，是该词更古老、更字面的用法
senses.example: The regiment spent a whole summer afield.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团整个夏天都在野外驻扎。
senses.why: This sense keeps the original picture unchanged: soldiers and hunters were literally in the fields, away from the town walls.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项原封不动地保留了最初的画面：士兵与猎人确实身处田野，远离城墙之内。

intro.en: Afield is a phrase worn down into one word: the Old English preposition on plus field, meaning in the field, later fused and extended to mean far from home.
intro.cn: afield 是一个短语磨损成的单词：古英语介词 on 加 field，意为「在田地里」，后来融合并引申为「远离家乡」。

items.en: Old English on meant on or in, and in casual speech it wore down to a single unstressed a-.
items.cn: 古英语 on 意为「在……上／中」，在口语中弱化为一个不重读的 a-。

items.en: Old English feld meant open country or unenclosed land, the ancestor of modern field.
items.cn: 古英语 feld 意为旷野或未围起的土地，是现代 field 的祖先。

items.en: The phrase on felde meant out in the open, used of grazing animals and of soldiers on campaign.
items.cn: 短语 on felde 意为「在旷野中」，用于放牧的牲畜与出征的士兵。

items.en: By the fourteenth century the two words had fused into afeld, written as a single adverb.
items.cn: 到十四世纪，两个词已融合为 afeld，写成一个副词。

items.en: Modern spelling restored the ie of field, and the adverb settled into far afield and further afield, meaning at a distance.
items.cn: 现代拼写恢复了 field 中的 ie，该副词固定用于 far afield 与 further afield，表示「在远处」。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the a- adverbs built from nouns; the near-meaning group lists other ways of saying far away.
note.cn: 形近组保留由名词构成的 a- 类副词；近义组列出其他表示「在远处」的说法。

entries.definition: In or to another place.

normalIntro.en: Afield is a-, on, plus field, open land: on the field, and therefore away from home.
normalIntro.cn: afield 就是 a-「在……上」加 field「田野」：在田野上，因此也就是离开家。

normal.en: The a- is the worn-down Old English on, the same a- you see in ashore, abroad and asleep.
normal.cn: 这个 a- 是古英语 on 的弱化形式，与 ashore、abroad、asleep 中的 a- 相同。

normal.en: Afield almost always follows far or further, so learn the pair far afield as one chunk.
normal.cn: afield 几乎总跟在 far 或 further 后面，所以把 far afield 当作一个整块来记。

normal.en: It is an adverb, never an adjective: say travellers from far afield, not afield travellers.
normal.cn: 它是副词，绝不作形容词：说 travellers from far afield，不说 afield travellers。

normal.en: Field means open land, so afield keeps the picture of stepping outside your own fence.
normal.cn: field 意为旷野，所以 afield 保留「走出自家围栏」的画面。

normal.en: Do not confuse afield with the field: the first tells where someone is, the second names the ground.
normal.cn: 别把 afield 与 the field 混淆：前者说人在哪里，后者指那块地。

abstract.en: Picture your own small plot, then the wide open country beyond its fence.
abstract.cn: 想象自家那一小块地，再想象围栏外辽阔的旷野。

abstract.en: Imagine a soldier leaving the town gate and sleeping under the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一个士兵走出城门，在天空下露宿。

abstract.en: Think of a letter that travelled three provinces to reach your desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一封跨越三个省才到你桌上的信。

examples.en: The magazine draws its writers from far afield.
examples.cn: 这份杂志的作者来自很远的地方。

examples.en: We had to look further afield for a supplier.
examples.cn: 我们不得不去更远的地方找供应商。

examples.en: Students who study afield often return with new ideas.
examples.cn: 到外地求学的学生回来时常带着新想法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿菲尔德」——阿（a）菲（fi）尔（el）德（d）：走出家门那片田野（field），就是到远处、在野外。

root: 古英语介词 on「在……上」加 feld「旷野、未围之地」构成短语 on felde「在田野中」，十四世纪融合为 afeld，现代拼写恢复 field 的 ie，成为副词 afield，并固定用于 far 或 further afield 表示「在远处」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses start from one step outside the fence: the literal one puts you in open country or on campaign, and the extended one simply measures how far that step took you from home.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都从「走出围栏的那一步」出发：字面义把你放在旷野或出征途中，引申义只是衡量这一步把你带得离家有多远。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: out of your own field, into the open
core.cn: 核心意象：离开自家那块地，走到外面的旷野

branches.en: Customers arriving from other provinces.
branches.cn: 客户从外省赶来。

branches.en: Searching beyond the usual local sources.
branches.cn: 到平常的本地渠道之外去寻找。

branches.en: Troops camping on open ground.
branches.cn: 部队在旷野扎营。

branches.en: Hunters working the fields all season.
branches.cn: 猎人整个季节都在田野里。

branches.en: Both put the subject outside the home fence.
branches.cn: 两者都把主体放在自家围栏之外。

intro.en: Afield belongs to a small English pattern where the preposition on wears down to a- and turns a noun into an adverb of place or state.
intro.cn: afield 属于英语中一个小构词模式：介词 on 弱化为 a-，把名词变成表示地点或状态的副词。

definition_zh: 参与式的；让人参与的；参与性民主的；参与式管理的；参与式研究的；参与式艺术的；参与式预算的；参与式体育的；参与式文化的
definition_en: organized so that members of a group take part in decisions, activities, or creation, rather than receiving them from above or watching them from outside
core_image: 圈子的门敞开着，里面的人都能伸手去改正在用的规则
scene: 社区花园不请设计师画定稿，而是让每户居民投票决定哪块地种什么。 Every household votes on what to plant, so the planning is participatory.
sceneCN: 这里 participatory 是「参与式的」（第 1 个义项：决策由成员共同做出，而非由上方定好）；句意：每户居民投票决定种什么，所以这种规划是参与式的。

pos.zh: 参与式的；让人参与的；共同参与的

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

derivatives.zh: 参与性的（更强调共同决策特征）

senses.title: Decisions made with the members
senses.titleCN: 由成员共同作出决定的
senses.definition: describing a process in which the people affected take part in making the decision rather than receiving it from above
senses.definitionCN: 指受影响的人参与作出决定、而不是从上方接受决定的流程
senses.example: The housing council adopted a participatory model for allocating flats.
senses.exampleCN: 住房委员会采用参与式模式分配住房。
senses.why: The suffix -ory means 'serving to' or 'having the function of'. Participatory marks a system whose function is to let feet enter the circle and move the pattern.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ory 意为“起……作用的”。participatory 标记的是一种制度，它的功能就是让脚踏进圈子并改变图案。

senses.title: Open to anyone affected
senses.definition: open in structure, so that outsiders and ordinary members can join, speak, and influence the outcome
senses.definitionCN: 结构上是开放的，外人与普通成员都能加入、发言并影响结果
senses.example: The planning meeting was unusually participatory for a city office.
senses.exampleCN: 对市政部门而言，这次规划会议开放得不同寻常。
senses.why: Here the adjective describes the door, not the decision. A participatory forum is one whose walls are low enough that a passer-by can lean in.
senses.whyCN: 这里形容词描述的是门，而不是决定。参与式论坛的墙足够低，路过的人也能探身进来。

senses.title: Of participatory democracy
senses.definition: relating to a model of democracy in which citizens take part directly in decisions, not only in periodic elections
senses.definitionCN: 指公民直接参与决策、而不只在定期选举中投票的民主模式
senses.example: Participatory democracy requires time that representative systems do not.
senses.exampleCN: 参与式民主需要代议制所不需要的时间。
senses.why: The circle is the polity. Where representative democracy asks citizens to choose who decides, this model asks them to sit in the circle themselves, so the word becomes a political label.
senses.whyCN: 这时的圈子是政治共同体。代议制民主请公民选择由谁决定，这种模式则请公民自己坐进圈里，于是这个词成了一个政治标签。

senses.title: Of shared management
senses.definition: relating to management in which employees help set goals, solve problems, and shape working rules
senses.definitionCN: 指员工参与设定目标、解决问题并制定工作规则的管理方式
senses.example: Participatory management failed here because no one owned the final call.
senses.exampleCN: 参与式管理在这里失败了，因为没有人对最终决定负责。
senses.why: A factory floor is also a circle. The adjective turns the org chart sideways: the boxes at the bottom are given lines back up into the decision.
senses.whyCN: 车间也是一个圈子。这个形容词把架构图横过来：底部的方框获得了指回决策的连线。

senses.title: Of research done with participants
senses.titleCN: 与参与者共同做的研究
senses.definition: relating to research in which the people studied help design the questions, collect data, and interpret results
senses.definitionCN: 指被研究者参与设计问题、收集数据与解释结果的研究方式
senses.example: Participatory research gave the village a say in what counted as success.
senses.exampleCN: 参与式研究让村民对“什么算成功”有了发言权。
senses.why: Researchers once stood outside the circle and measured it. This sense puts them inside, so the people being studied become co-authors of the finding.
senses.whyCN: 研究者从前站在圈外测量圈子。这个义项把他们放进圈内，于是被研究的人成了研究结论的共同作者。

senses.title: Of art that needs the audience
senses.definition: relating to art whose meaning or existence depends on the audience doing something, not only looking
senses.definitionCN: 指意义或存在依赖观众动手做事、而不只是观看的艺术
senses.example: The participatory installation asked visitors to write on the walls.
senses.exampleCN: 这件参与式装置请参观者在墙上写字。
senses.why: A painting can be finished by the artist. A participatory work is unfinished until a foot enters the circle, which makes the viewer a material of the piece.
senses.whyCN: 一幅画可以由艺术家完成。参与式作品在有人踏进圈子之前都未完成，这使观众成了作品的材料。

senses.title: Of budgeting by residents
senses.definition: relating to a budget process in which residents decide how part of a public budget is spent
senses.definitionCN: 指由居民决定部分公共预算如何使用的预算流程
senses.example: Participatory budgeting moved the playground repair to the top of the list.
senses.exampleCN: 参与式预算把操场维修提到了清单最前面。
senses.why: Money is the clearest test of the open door. If residents can move a real sum, the participation is not a consultation but a hand on the lever.
senses.whyCN: 钱是检验门是否敞开的最清楚方式。如果居民能挪动一笔真实的款项，参与就不是征询意见，而是手真的握上了操纵杆。

senses.title: Of sport played, not watched
senses.titleCN: 亲自参与而非观看的体育
senses.definition: relating to sport that people play themselves, as opposed to professional sport watched by spectators
senses.definitionCN: 指人们亲自从事的体育运动，相对于观众观看的职业赛事
senses.example: Funding shifted from stadiums to participatory sport in schools.
senses.exampleCN: 资金从体育场转向了学校的参与性体育。
senses.why: Here the contrast is between feet in the circle and eyes outside it. The word classifies an activity by who is doing it, not by how organized it is.
senses.whyCN: 这里的对比是圈里的脚与圈外的眼。这个词按“谁在做”来分类活动，而不是按组织程度。

senses.title: Of a culture that remakes its content
senses.titleCN: 会改写自身内容的文化
senses.definition: relating to a culture in which fans and users produce, remix, and circulate content rather than only consuming it
senses.definitionCN: 指粉丝与用户生产、混编并传播内容、而不只是消费内容的文化
senses.example: Fan translation is a participatory culture in its purest form.
senses.exampleCN: 粉丝翻译是参与式文化最纯粹的形式。
senses.why: The suffix now attaches to culture itself. When readers become writers, the circle stops having a clear outside, and the adjective marks that blurred boundary.
senses.whyCN: 这个后缀现在挂到了文化本身上。当读者变成作者，圈子不再有清楚的外面，这个形容词标记的正是那条模糊的边界。

intro.en: Participatory is the adjective of participate, formed with -ory from Latin -orius, a suffix meaning 'serving for, having the function of'. The base is Latin participare, from particeps 'part-taking', itself pars 'part' plus capere 'take'. English built the adjective in the 19th century; it first described political arrangements and later spread to management, research, art, and digital culture.
intro.cn: participatory 是 participate 的形容词，由 -ory（拉丁 -orius，意为“用于……的、具有……功能的”）构成。基础是拉丁语 participare，出自 particeps“拿取一份的”，而 particeps 又是 pars“部分”加 capere“拿取”。英语在 19 世纪造出这个形容词，最初描述政治安排，后来扩展到管理、研究、艺术与数字文化。

items.en: The suffix -orius in Latin forms adjectives of function, as in amatorius 'serving for love' and obligatorius 'binding'. English -ory keeps that sense of 'designed to do this'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 -orius 构成表功能的形容词，如 amatorius“用于爱的”、obligatorius“有约束力的”。英语 -ory 保留了“被设计来做这件事”的含义。

items.en: The adjective appears in English in the 19th century, mainly in political writing about schemes in which citizens share in government.
items.cn: 这个形容词在 19 世纪进入英语，主要用于讨论公民共同参与治理的政治写作。

items.en: Management theory, development practice, and adult education all adopt it: participatory management, participatory research, participatory rural appraisal.
items.cn: 管理学、发展实践与成人教育都采用了它：参与式管理、参与式研究、参与式农村评估。

items.en: Participatory democracy becomes a slogan of student and civic movements, fixing the word as a positive political label.
items.cn: 20 世纪 60 至 70 年代，参与式民主成为学生运动与公民运动的口号，使这个词固定为一个正面的政治标签。

items.en: Media studies apply it to fan production and online platforms: participatory culture, participatory media. The suffix now marks a blurring line between producer and audience.
items.cn: 20 世纪 90 年代至 2000 年代，媒介研究把它用于粉丝生产与网络平台：参与式文化、参与式媒介。这个后缀此时标记的是生产者与受众之间正在模糊的界线。

items.en: The -ory here is not the -ory of 'laboratory' (a place) or the -ory of 'sensory' (belonging to). It is the function suffix: a participatory system is one whose function is participation.
items.cn: 这里的 -ory 不是 laboratory（地点）的 -ory，也不是 sensory（属于）的 -ory，而是表功能的后缀：参与式制度的功用就是“参与”。

note.en: The first group follows the particip- family and marks the near neighbour that only shares the suffix. The second group compares adjectives for things opened to members, to the public, to collaborators, or to users.
note.cn: 第一组沿着 particip- 词族，并标出一个只是共享后缀的近邻。第二组比较表示“对成员开放”“对公众开放”“协作的”“动手的”几个形容词。

entries.definition: to take part in something. The adjective participatory adds -ory to describe a system built to make this happen.
entries.definitionCN: 参加某事。形容词 participatory 加 -ory，用来描述一个被设计成让这种事发生的体系。

entries.definition: the act or share of taking part. It names what happens, while participatory names the design that invites it.
entries.definitionCN: 参与的行为或份额。它命名发生的事，而 participatory 命名邀请这件事发生的设计。

entries.definition: a person who takes part. It is a countable role, whereas participatory is a property of a process.
entries.definitionCN: 参与的人。它是可数的角色，而 participatory 是流程的属性。

entries.definition: relating to a participle. It looks close to participatory but belongs to grammar, not to decision-making.
entries.definitionCN: 与分词有关的。它看起来接近 participatory，却属于语法领域，与决策无关。

entries.definition: deliberately taking in all groups, especially those usually excluded. It stresses who is admitted, while participatory stresses what they do once admitted.
entries.definitionCN: 有意把一切群体纳入，尤其是不常被纳入的群体。它强调谁被接纳，而 participatory 强调被接纳后他们做了什么。

entries.definition: based on the principle that power belongs to the people, usually through voting. It is the wider constitutional idea; participatory names one method of realizing it.
entries.definitionCN: 基于权力属于人民的原则，通常通过投票实现。它是更宽的宪制理念，participatory 是实现它的一种方法。

entries.definition: involving two or more parties working jointly on a task. It stresses joint labour, while participatory stresses shared authority over decisions.
entries.definitionCN: 由两方或多方共同完成一项任务。它强调共同劳动，而 participatory 强调决策权的共享。

entries.definition: involving direct practical activity. It describes the mode of work, not the distribution of decision-making power.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及直接的实践活动。它描述工作方式，而不描述决策权的分配。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: -ory as a function suffix, participare, particeps, the 19th-century political origin, and the four -ory words that are not this -ory.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：-ory 作功能后缀、participare、particeps、19 世纪的政治来源，以及四个不属于这个 -ory 的词。

normal.en: -ory means 'serving to': a participatory system is a system whose job is to let people take part.
normal.cn: -ory 意为“用于……”：参与式体系就是一个以让人参与为职责的体系。

normal.en: The base is particeps, 'part-taker': participatory design gives every member a part to take.
normal.cn: 基础是 particeps“拿取一份的人”：参与式设计给每个成员一份可以拿的东西。

normal.en: The word rose in 19th-century political writing about citizens sharing in government, then moved into offices, clinics, and studios.
normal.cn: 这个词兴起于 19 世纪关于公民共同治理的政治写作，之后进入办公室、诊所与工作室。

normal.en: Do not confuse -ory here with the -ory of laboratory (a place) or sensory (belonging to): this one says 'designed for'.
normal.cn: 不要把这里的 -ory 与 laboratory（地点）或 sensory（属于）的 -ory 混同：这里是“为……而设计”。

normal.en: Participatory democracy, management, research, art, and culture are five arenas where the same open door is installed.
normal.cn: 参与式民主、管理、研究、艺术与文化，是同一扇敞开的门被装进去的五个场所。

abstract.en: A door that is open is not the same as a room that is shared; the adjective names the hinge, not the furniture.
abstract.cn: 门开着不等于房间被共享；这个形容词命名的是合页，而不是家具。

abstract.en: A rule written by everyone is slower to finish and harder to overturn.
abstract.cn: 由所有人写成的规则完成得更慢，也更难被推翻。

abstract.en: When the audience holds the brush, the painting no longer has an outside.
abstract.cn: 当观众握住画笔，这幅画就不再有一个“外面”。

examples.en: The school adopted a participatory approach to curriculum design.
examples.cn: 学校在课程设计上采用了参与式方法。

examples.en: Participatory budgeting gave residents control over a fifth of the budget.
examples.cn: 参与式预算让居民掌控了五分之一的预算。

examples.en: The exhibition is participatory: visitors build part of the work.
examples.cn: 这场展览是参与式的：参观者会搭建作品的一部分。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「帕提西破特瑞」——帕提把门推开，让圈里每个人都“破”例伸手改规则 → participatory 参与式的；让人参与的（只借音，不表词源）

root: 拉丁 participare「分享、参与」，出自 particeps「拿取一份的人」（pars「部分」+ capere「拿取」）；后缀 -ory（拉丁 -orius）表功能，意为“用于……的”。核心是「把圈子的门敞开，让成员的手伸进规则里」。同族含 participate、participation、participant；perception 共享 capere 但前缀不同。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of participatory all describe an open door in a circle. What changes is the circle — a council, a workplace, a research team, a gallery, a budget, a playing field, or a fandom — and whether the adjective describes the decision, the openness, or the culture.
sensesIntro.cn: participatory 的九个义项都描述圈子上的一扇敞开的门。变化的是圈子本身——议事会、工作场所、研究团队、美术馆、预算、球场或粉丝社群——以及形容词描述的是决定、开放程度，还是文化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circle whose door is open, so that members can reach in and change the rules while they are being used.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个门敞开的圈子，成员可以在规则还在使用时伸手进去修改。

chain: THE DESIGN IS NAMED FOR THIS

branches.en: THE OPEN PROCESS: decisions made with members, and a structure open to anyone affected.
branches.cn: 开放的流程：与成员共同作出决定，以及向所有受影响者开放的结构。

branches.en: GOVERNANCE AND WORK: participatory democracy in the polity, participatory management at the workplace.
branches.cn: 治理与工作：政治共同体中的参与式民主，工作场所中的参与式管理。

branches.en: KNOWLEDGE: research in which the studied help design the questions and read the results.
branches.cn: 知识：由被研究者参与设计问题与解读结果的研究。

branches.en: CULTURE AND MONEY: art that needs the audience to act, and budgets that residents can move.
branches.cn: 文化与金钱：需要观众行动的艺术，以及居民可以挪动的预算。

branches.en: PLAY AND PRODUCTION: sport played rather than watched, and a culture that remakes its own content.
branches.cn: 游戏与生产：亲自从事而非观看的体育，以及会改写自身内容的文化。

intro.en: Participatory is participate plus -ory, from Latin -orius. The stem is participat-, from participare, which rests on particeps (pars 'part' + capere 'take'). The adjective is a 19th-century English formation; the Latin language had no participatory.
intro.cn: participatory 是 participate 加 -ory（拉丁 -orius）。词干是 participat-，出自 participare，其基础为 particeps（pars“部分”+ capere“拿取”）。这个形容词是 19 世纪英语的构词，拉丁语本身并没有 participatory。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is pars 'part', capere 'take', particeps 'part-taker', participare 'to share'. Latin -orius formed adjectives of function, the source of English -ory.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 pars“部分”、capere“拿取”、particeps“拿取一份的人”、participare“分享”。拉丁 -orius 构成表功能的形容词，是英语 -ory 的来源。

items.meaning: designed so that people take part
items.meaningCN: 被设计成让人参与的（-ory 功能形容词）
items.example: The workshop used a participatory method.
items.exampleCN: 工作坊采用了参与式方法。

items.example: All residents may participate.
items.exampleCN: 所有居民都可以参与。

items.meaning: the act or share of taking part
items.meaningCN: 参与的行为或份额（-ion 动作名词）
items.example: Participation was higher than expected.
items.exampleCN: 参与程度高于预期。

items.example: Every participant signed the form.
items.exampleCN: 每位参与者都签了表。

items.meaningCN: 以共同决策为特征的（-ive 倾向形容词）
items.example: The team prefers a participative style.
items.exampleCN: 这个团队偏好参与性的风格。

items.example: He was a silent participator in the debate.
items.exampleCN: 他是这场辩论中沉默的参加者。

items.meaning: a piece of a whole, or a share
items.example: Each part has its own label.
items.exampleCN: 每一部分都有自己的标签。

items.structure: Old French parçonier, from Latin partitionem
items.meaning: one who shares an activity or business
items.meaningCN: 共同从事活动或经营的人；伙伴
items.example: The two firms became partners in 2010.
items.exampleCN: 这两家公司在 2010 年成为合作伙伴。

items.meaning: a taking in through the senses
items.example: Depth perception develops early in infancy.
items.exampleCN: 深度知觉在婴儿期很早就发展起来。

latinEntries.meaning: serving for, having the function of

definition_zh: 研究设计；研究方案；研究架构
definition_en: the overall plan that specifies how a study will collect, measure and analyse evidence in order to answer a research question
core_image: 桌上摊开一张流程图，顶端写着研究问题，往下分出抽样、测量、时点与统计四列，角落贴满修订便签
scene: 开题会上，导师把一张流程图铺在桌面，问题写在顶端，往下分出抽样、工具、时点与统计四列，桌角还压着一叠修改稿。 A sound research design states whom to study, what to measure and when to stop.
sceneCN: 这里指一项研究的总体方案（第 1 个义项：研究的总体计划）；句意为严谨的研究设计会说明研究谁、测量什么以及何时停止。图中可辨识物件：流程图、研究问题卡片、抽样框、测量工具、时间轴、统计表。

pos.zh: 研究设计；研究方案；研究架构

derivatives.zh: 由古法语 recerche 而来，义为「研究；调查」
由研究动词加表示施动者的词尾构成，义为「研究者」
由拉丁语 designare 经法语而来，义为「设计；方案」
由设计动词加表示施动者的词尾构成，义为「设计者」
由表示「重新」的前缀加设计动词构成，义为「重新设计」

senses.title: The overall plan of a study
senses.definition: the complete plan that states the question, the evidence needed and the steps for gathering it
senses.definitionCN: 说明研究问题、所需证据与收集步骤的完整计划
senses.example: The research design must be approved before any data are collected.
senses.exampleCN: 在任何数据收集之前，研究设计必须先获批准。
senses.why: A study is built twice, once on paper and once in the field, and this sense names the paper version.
senses.whyCN: 研究要建两次，一次在纸上，一次在现场，这个义项指纸上的那一版。

senses.title: The choice of a research strategy
senses.definition: the decision to use quantitative, qualitative or mixed methods and the reasons given for that choice
senses.definitionCN: 决定采用定量、定性或混合方法，并说明这样选择的理由
senses.example: Their research design combines interviews with a large survey.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的研究设计把访谈与大规模问卷结合起来。
senses.why: Before any instrument is chosen, the study must decide what kind of evidence will count as an answer.
senses.whyCN: 在选定任何工具之前，研究必须先决定什么样的证据才算答案。

senses.title: The arrangement of comparison and control
senses.definition: the way participants are assigned to groups and the way rival explanations are ruled out
senses.definitionCN: 安排参与者如何分组，以及如何排除其他可能的解释
senses.example: An experimental research design assigns participants to groups at random.
senses.exampleCN: 实验性研究设计把参与者随机分配到各组。
senses.why: A claim about cause needs a contrast, and the plan must build that contrast before the first measurement.
senses.whyCN: 关于因果的主张需要一个对照，而方案必须在第一次测量之前把这个对照搭好。

senses.title: The plan for selecting participants
senses.definition: the specification of the population, the sampling frame and the rules for including or excluding cases
senses.definitionCN: 明确总体、抽样框以及纳入或排除个案的标准
senses.example: The research design names the population before the sample is drawn.
senses.exampleCN: 研究设计在抽取样本之前就写明总体。
senses.why: Who enters the study decides what the study can later say about the world, so selection belongs to the plan.
senses.whyCN: 谁进入研究决定了研究之后能对世界说什么，因此取样属于方案的一部分。

senses.title: The timing and sequence of measurement
senses.definition: the schedule of when data are collected, including cross-sectional or longitudinal choices
senses.definitionCN: 数据收集的时间安排，包括横断面或纵贯式的选择
senses.example: A longitudinal research design follows the same households for ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 纵贯式研究设计追踪同一批家庭长达十年。
senses.why: Time is a design variable: measuring once and measuring repeatedly answer different questions.
senses.whyCN: 时间是设计变量：测一次与反复测回答的是不同的问题。

senses.title: The plan for instruments and measures
senses.definition: the selection and definition of questionnaires, tests, observation schedules or interview guides
senses.definitionCN: 选定并界定问卷、测验、观察记录表或访谈提纲
senses.example: The research design fixes the wording of every item in advance.
senses.exampleCN: 研究设计预先固定每个题项的字面表述。
senses.why: An instrument produces the numbers or texts a study will analyse, so its wording is part of the architecture.
senses.whyCN: 工具产生研究将要分析的数字或文本，因此它的措辞属于架构的一部分。

senses.title: The written protocol
senses.definition: the document that records procedures, materials and decision rules in enough detail for another team to repeat the work
senses.definitionCN: 把程序、材料与决策规则记录到另一支团队可以复做的详细文件
senses.example: Reviewers asked for the full research design as a separate document.
senses.exampleCN: 评审人要求把完整的研究设计作为单独文件提交。
senses.why: A plan that stays in someone's head cannot be reviewed, funded or repeated, so it is written down.
senses.whyCN: 留在个人脑子里的方案无法被评审、资助或复做，因此必须写成文件。

senses.title: The quality of the plan
senses.definition: the extent to which the plan protects internal and external validity against foreseeable threats
senses.definitionCN: 方案在可预见的威胁面前保护内部效度与外部效度的程度
senses.example: A weak research design cannot be repaired by a large sample.
senses.exampleCN: 薄弱的研究设计无法靠大样本补救。
senses.why: Design choices set the ceiling on what analysis can achieve, and later statistics can only work below that ceiling.
senses.whyCN: 设计选择给分析划定了上限，后来的统计只能在那个上限之下发挥作用。

intro.en: Research design joins a French word for close searching to a Latin word for marking out. The phrase itself is a modern social-science compound.
intro.cn: 这个术语把表示「仔细搜寻」的法语词与表示「划出标记」的拉丁词组合在一起，本身是现代社会科学的复合词。

items.en: Recerchier meant to search closely, built from an intensive prefix and cerchier, to search.
items.cn: 古法语 recerchier 意为仔细搜寻，由加强语气的前缀加 cerchier「搜寻」构成。

items.en: Cerchier descended from circare, to go about or wander, which came from circus, a circle.
items.cn: cerchier 源出 circare「四处走动、游走」，而 circare 又来自 circus「圆圈」。

items.en: English adopted research in the sixteenth century for close inquiry; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪引入 research 表示深入探究；确切的首见年代不确定。

items.en: Designare meant to mark out or designate, from de- out of and signum a sign.
items.cn: designare 意为划出、指定，由 de-「取出」加 signum「记号」构成。

items.en: French dess(e)in carried both drawing and intention, and English kept the plan and the purpose together.
items.cn: 法语 dess(e)in 同时带有「绘图」与「意图」，英语把方案与目的合在一起保留下来。

items.en: Statistics and the social sciences joined the two nouns into a name for the architecture of an inquiry.
items.cn: 统计学与社会科学把这两个名词组合成指研究架构的名称。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like this phrase; the second group names neighbouring ideas of planning and inquiry.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与本术语相近；第二组是与「规划、探究」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The first half, naming systematic inquiry.
entries.definitionCN: 前半，指系统的探究。

entries.definition: The second half, naming a plan or a marked-out arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 后半，指方案或划定的安排。

entries.definition: To mark out or name officially; it shares the Latin signum with design.
entries.definitionCN: 指正式指定或命名；与「设计」共享拉丁语 signum。

entries.definition: To plan again after the first plan has been tested.
entries.definitionCN: 指在初版方案受检验后重新规划。

entries.definition: Able to be investigated with available evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 指可以用现有证据加以探究的。

entries.definition: The study of methods and the reasoned system behind them.
entries.definitionCN: 指对方法的研究及其背后的理据体系。

entries.definition: A written procedure for carrying out a study.
entries.definitionCN: 指开展研究用的成文程序。

entries.definition: The part of a design that decides who will be studied.
entries.definitionCN: 指设计中决定研究谁的那一部分。

entries.definition: A controlled test arranged to reveal a causal relation.
entries.definitionCN: 指为揭示因果关系而安排的对照检验。

entries.definition: A structured collection of information from many respondents.
entries.definitionCN: 指从众多受访者处系统收集信息。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations work through the real parts, word family and common phrases behind this term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想依托这个术语背后真实的构词部件、同族词与常见搭配。

normal.en: Research and design are two ordinary words, and the phrase becomes technical only when they are joined.
normal.cn: 研究和设计都是普通词，只有组合起来才成为专业术语。

normal.en: The Latin signum behind design also gives designate and signal, so the word begins with a mark.
normal.cn: 「设计」背后的拉丁语 signum 也构成「指定」与「信号」两个词，这个词从「记号」开始。

normal.en: A design is approved before the study starts, just as a building plan is approved before the first brick.
normal.cn: 研究设计在开工前获批，正如建筑图纸在第一块砖之前获批。

normal.en: The word research carries the idea of searching again and again, not of finding once.
normal.cn: 研究一词带着反复搜寻的意思，而不是一次找到。

normal.en: Longitudinal, cross-sectional and experimental are the usual labels attached to a design.
normal.cn: 纵贯、横断面与实验是贴在研究设计上的常见标签。

abstract.en: A design is a promise made to future readers about what will count as evidence.
abstract.cn: 研究设计是对未来读者作出的承诺：什么才算证据。

abstract.en: The plan draws a fence around the study, and everything outside the fence is called a limitation.
abstract.cn: 方案在研究的四周画出围栏，围栏之外的一切后来都叫局限。

abstract.en: Two studies can use the same words and still differ entirely, because the architecture behind them differs.
abstract.cn: 两项研究可以用同样的词，却因背后的架构不同而完全不同。

examples.en: The team revised the research design after the pilot study.
examples.cn: 试点研究之后，团队修改了研究设计。

examples.en: A research design should state how missing data will be handled.
examples.cn: 研究设计应说明缺失数据将如何处理。

examples.en: The journal now asks authors to submit the research design with the manuscript.
examples.cn: 该期刊现在要求作者随稿提交研究设计。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「研究」加「设计」——先想清研究谁、测什么、何时停，再动手；图纸定得清楚，后面才不返工。

root: 古法语 recerchier「仔细搜寻」← 拉丁 circare「四处走动」← circus「圆圈」；拉丁 designare「划出、指定」← de-「取出」+ signum「记号」，经法语 design 进入英语；两词组合成现代研究术语。首见年代不确定不影响构词来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the whole plan to its parts: overall blueprint, strategy, comparison and control, sampling, timing, instruments, written protocol, and the quality of the plan.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从整体方案走向各部分：总体蓝图、策略选择、比较与控制、取样、时点、工具、成文方案，以及方案的严密程度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flow chart on a desk, with the research question at the top and branches for sample, measure, time and analysis.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上一张流程图，研究问题在顶端，向下分出样本、测量、时间与分析四支。

branches.en: THE WHOLE ARCHITECTURE: the plan that contains every later decision.
branches.cn: 整体架构：容纳后续所有决策的方案。

branches.en: THE DECLARED STRATEGY: the chosen method and the document that records it.
branches.cn: 已宣告的策略：选定的方法以及记录它的文件。

branches.en: THE BUILT CONTRAST: groups and controls arranged so that a cause can be tested.
branches.cn: 搭好的对照：通过分组与控制使因果得以检验。

branches.en: THE ENTRY AND MEASUREMENT RULES: who is studied and with which instruments.
branches.cn: 进入与测量规则：研究谁、用什么工具。

branches.en: THE SCHEDULE AND ITS STRENGTH: when measurement happens, and how well the plan resists threats.
branches.cn: 时点与强度：何时测量，以及方案抵御威胁的能力。

dict_mnemonic.text: endearment ＝ endear（使受喜爱：en- ＋ dear）＋ -ment（名词后缀）＝「使人变得亲爱的那句话或那个举动」。动词 endear 使受喜爱，形容词 endearing 讨人喜欢的，副词 endearingly 惹人喜爱地，词根 dear 亲爱的、昂贵的（古英语 deore 珍贵）。三类用法：爱称 a term of endearment 一个爱称、terms of endearment 亲昵称呼；情话 whisper an endearment 低声说情话；举动 a small endearment 一个小小的亲昵举动。常见搭配 use endearments 使用爱称。注意 endearment 是名词，endearing 是形容词，endear 是动词，三者不要混用；dear 既是亲爱的也是昂贵的，同一词源。
