definition_zh: 引力；万有引力作用力；（口语）不可抗拒的吸引力
definition_en: the attractive force between bodies with mass, or a figurative irresistible pull
core_image: 月亮被一根看不见的力线牵在地球旁边，力线的箭头指向地心
scene: 讲解月亮为何绕地球转，你说 Gravitational force keeps the moon in orbit.
sceneCN: 这里 gravitational force 指「有质量的物体之间的吸引力」（第 1 个义项：两质量之间的引力）；句意为引力使月球保持在轨道上。图中可辨识物件：地球、月球、指向地心的力箭头、轨道弧线。

pos.zh: 引力；万有引力作用力；（口语）不可抗拒的吸引力

collocations.phrase: the gravitational force of the earth
the gravitational force between two masses

senses.title: The attractive force between masses
senses.titleCN: 有质量物体之间的吸引力
senses.definition: the force with which any two bodies attract each other because of their mass
senses.definitionCN: 任何两个有质量物体因质量而相互吸引的力
senses.example: Gravitational force keeps the moon in orbit.
senses.exampleCN: 引力使月球保持在轨道上。
senses.why: the phrase spells out what gravitation names in the abstract: a force, acting between masses, and always attractive.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把 gravitation 抽象指称的东西说清楚：一种力，作用于质量之间，且总是吸引。

senses.title: The inverse-square law
senses.titleCN: 平方反比定律：力随距离平方衰减
senses.definition: the law stating that the force falls with the square of the distance between the bodies
senses.definitionCN: 力随两物体间距离的平方而减小的定律
senses.example: The gravitational force drops to a quarter when the distance doubles.
senses.exampleCN: 距离加倍时引力减到四分之一。
senses.why: geometry does the work: the same influence spread over a sphere four times larger is four times weaker.
senses.whyCN: 起作用的是几何：同样的影响摊到四倍大的球面上，就弱了四倍。

senses.title: Weight as a local force
senses.titleCN: 重量：物体在特定引力场中受到的力
senses.definition: the force a body experiences in a particular gravitational field, measured as its weight
senses.definitionCN: 物体在特定引力场中受到、以重量计量的力
senses.example: The gravitational force on the probe is weaker far from the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 远离太阳时，探测器受到的引力更弱。
senses.why: weight is the local reading of the force: the same body feels different gravitational force on different planets.
senses.whyCN: 重量是这种力的局部读数：同一个物体在不同行星上感受到不同的引力。

senses.title: The tidal difference
senses.titleCN: 潮汐力：物体两端受力不均
senses.definition: the difference in gravitational force across a body, which stretches it
senses.definitionCN: 横跨一个物体两端的引力差异，会把它拉长
senses.example: The gravitational force of the moon raises two tides a day.
senses.exampleCN: 月球的引力每天造成两次潮汐。
senses.why: a tide appears because the near side is pulled harder than the far side, so the difference matters as much as the total.
senses.whyCN: 潮汐的出现是因为近侧比远侧被拉得更紧，因此差值跟总量同样重要。

senses.title: The weakest of the four forces
senses.titleCN: 四种基本力中最弱、作用距离最长的一种
senses.definition: the weakest of the four fundamental interactions, yet the one with unlimited range
senses.definitionCN: 四种基本相互作用中最弱、但作用距离不受限的一种
senses.example: Gravitational force is weak, but it never cancels out.
senses.exampleCN: 引力很弱，但它从不相互抵消。
senses.why: it is weak per particle and strong in bulk: mass adds up, and there is no negative mass to cancel it.
senses.whyCN: 就单个粒子而言它很弱，成团时却很强：质量会累加，又没有负质量来抵消。

senses.title: Balancing an orbit
senses.titleCN: 轨道中与运动相平衡的力
senses.definition: the force that supplies the inward pull needed to keep a body in orbit
senses.definitionCN: 为维持天体在轨道上所需的向内拉力
senses.example: The gravitational force provides exactly the pull the orbit needs.
senses.exampleCN: 引力恰好提供了轨道所需的拉力。
senses.why: an orbit is a balance: the inward force bends the path just enough that the body never lands and never leaves.
senses.whyCN: 轨道是一种平衡：向内的力把路径弯得刚好，使天体既不落地也不飞走。

senses.title: Figurative: an irresistible pull
senses.titleCN: 比喻义：不可抗拒的吸引力
senses.definition: a figurative use for a person or thing that draws others irresistibly
senses.definitionCN: 比喻某人或某物不可抗拒地吸引他人
senses.example: The old harbour exerts a gravitational force on the whole town.
senses.exampleCN: 旧港对整座城镇有一种引力般的吸引。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps two features: the pull is invisible and it acts at a distance.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留两个特征：拉力不可见，且能隔空起作用。

senses.title: A force only by approximation
senses.titleCN: 广义相对论中的再解释：力只是近似说法
senses.definition: the modern note that in general relativity this 'force' is a description of curved paths, not a push or pull
senses.definitionCN: 现代注脚：在广义相对论中，这个「力」只是对弯曲路径的描述，而非推或拉
senses.example: In general relativity the gravitational force is a bookkeeping device.
senses.exampleCN: 在广义相对论中，引力只是一种记账手段。
senses.why: the phrase survives because it is convenient, even though the deeper theory replaces the pull with geometry.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语因方便而留存，尽管更深的理论已用几何取代拉力。

intro.en: Gravitational force joins gravitational, from Latin gravitas 'weight', to force, from Latin fortis 'strong' through Old French. The phrase is a modern physics label. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: gravitational force 把出自拉丁 gravitas「重量」的 gravitational 与经古法语来自拉丁 fortis「强」的 force 并置。这个短语是近代物理标签。年代均为约数。

items.en: Gravis 'heavy, weighty' is the root of gravitas and of the whole gravity family; its Indo-European origin is a reconstruction.
items.cn: gravis「重的、有分量的」是 gravitas 与整个 gravity 词族的词根；其印欧来源属重构。

items.en: Fortis meant 'strong, powerful', and gave English force through Old French; the noun force names strength in action.
items.cn: fortis 意为「强的、有力的」，经古法语给出英语 force；名词 force 指起作用的力量。

items.en: Gravitational force became standard once Newtonian mechanics needed an explicit name for the interaction, distinct from gravitation as a phenomenon.
items.cn: 当牛顿力学需要一个明确的名称来指这种相互作用、并与作为现象的 gravitation 区分时，gravitational force 成为标准说法。

items.en: Later work on tides and orbits attached the phrase to local differences and to the balance that keeps a body in orbit.
items.cn: 后来关于潮汐与轨道的工作把这个短语用于局部差异，以及维持天体在轨道上的平衡。

items.en: General relativity kept the phrase as a convenient label while denying that it names a fundamental push or pull.
items.cn: 广义相对论保留这个短语作为方便标签，同时否认它指某种基本的推或拉。

items.en: Root uncertainty: the Indo-European shapes behind gravis and fortis are reconstructions. First-date uncertainty only: the earliest printed use of the exact phrase gravitational force is not recorded.
items.cn: 词根存疑：gravis 与 fortis 背后的印欧形态均属重构。仅首见年代存疑：gravitational force 这一确切短语的最早印刷记录不明。

note.en: Group one holds the weight-family words that are easily swapped; group two holds the related force terms and the figurative near-equivalents.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「重」词族、容易互换的词；第二组是相关力的术语与比喻近义词。

entries.definition: The abstract noun for the phenomenon; gravitational force is the explicit phrase for the interaction itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指现象或理论的抽象名词；gravitational force 是明确指这种相互作用的短语。

entries.definition: The adjective alone cannot name the force; it needs a noun such as force, wave or lens.
entries.definitionCN: 这个形容词本身不能指该力，须带 force、wave、lens 等名词。

entries.definition: The common noun for the force, also meaning seriousness; the longer phrase is more precise in physics.
entries.definitionCN: 指该力的常用名词，也指严肃；较长的短语在物理中更精确。

entries.definition: The force a body feels in a given field; it is the local value of gravitational force, not the general relation.
entries.definitionCN: 物体在给定场中受到的力；它是引力的局部取值，不是普遍关系。

entries.definition: The difference in gravitational force between two points, which stretches an object; it is a special case, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 两点之间引力的差值，会拉长物体；是特例，非同义词。

entries.definition: The everyday word for an attracting action; the physics phrase is its technical counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指吸引动作的日常词；物理短语是其技术对应语。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: gravitational 'of weight' + force 'strength': the strength that comes with mass.
normal.cn: gravitational「关于重的」+ force「力」：随质量而来的力。

normal.en: Fixed collocations: the gravitational force of the earth, between two masses.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：地球的引力、两个质量之间的引力。

normal.en: It falls off as the square of the distance.
normal.cn: 它随距离的平方衰减。

normal.en: The family runs gravitation, gravity, gravitate, gravitational wave.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 gravitation、gravity、gravitate、gravitational wave。

normal.en: Weight is the local reading of the force.
normal.cn: 重量是这种力的局部读数。

abstract.en: Picture a cord tied from the moon to the centre of the earth.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳把月亮系在地心。

abstract.en: Picture two dancers turning around each other without touching.
abstract.cn: 想象两个舞者彼此绕行却不相触。

abstract.en: Picture an old harbour that nobody can quite leave.
abstract.cn: 想象一座谁都舍不得离开的旧港。

examples.en: The gravitational force between two masses grows as they come closer.
examples.cn: 两个质量之间的引力随距离缩短而增大。

examples.en: Astronauts feel a weaker gravitational force on the moon.
examples.cn: 宇航员在月球上感受到的引力更弱。

examples.en: The gravitational force of a black hole bends light around it.
examples.cn: 黑洞的引力使周围的光弯曲。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「gravitational（引力的）+ force（力）」——由质量产生的拉力 → 引力

root: 拉丁 gravitas「重量」← gravis「重的」+ 拉丁 fortis「强」经古法语 force；近代物理短语，用于指质量之间的吸引作用。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one pull: masses attract, distance weakens it, weight measures it locally, tides reveal its difference, it is the weakest of four forces, orbits balance it, people feel it as charm and modern physics calls it geometry.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种拉力展开：质量相吸；距离使它减弱；重量是它的局部度量；潮汐显出它的差值；它是四种力中最弱的；轨道靠它平衡；人们把它感受为魅力；现代物理则称它为几何。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow drawn from the moon toward the earth's centre.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支从月球指向地心的箭头。

branches.en: THE FORCE ITSELF: always attractive, weak per particle, unlimited in range.
branches.cn: 力本身：总是吸引，单粒子很弱，作用距离不受限。

branches.en: THE LAW OF DISTANCE: the inverse square.
branches.cn: 距离的定律：平方反比。

branches.en: LOCAL READINGS: weight at one point, tidal difference across a body.
branches.cn: 局部读数：某一点的重量，横跨物体的潮汐差。

branches.en: BALANCE AND BOOKKEEPING: what holds an orbit, and what relativity renames as geometry.
branches.cn: 平衡与记账：维持轨道的东西，以及相对论改称为几何的东西。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: an invisible pull that acts at a distance.
branches.cn: 比喻：隔空起作用的无形拉力。

intro.en: The phrase is an English adjective plus a French-borrowed noun, both from Latin roots; the adjective carries the weight family, the noun the strength family.
intro.cn: 这个短语是英语形容词加一个法语借入的名词，两者都源自拉丁词根；形容词带「重」词族，名词带「强」词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin gravis gives gravity and gravitation; Latin fortis gives force, fortify and fortress.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 gravis 给出 gravity 与 gravitation；拉丁 fortis 给出 force、fortify、fortress。

items.example: The root supplies the first element of gravitational.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供 gravitational 的第一成分。

items.example: Gravitation is built on this stem.
items.exampleCN: gravitation 建立在这个词干上。

items.example: The suffix forms the abstract noun gravitation.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成抽象名词 gravitation。

items.example: Gravitational means of gravitation.
items.exampleCN: gravitational 意为引力的。

items.example: The noun entered English through Old French.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词经古法语进入英语。

items.example: The root also gives fortify.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根还给出 fortify。

items.example: The adjective is required before force.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词在 force 前是必需的。

items.example: The shorter noun is the everyday form.
items.exampleCN: 较短的名词是日常形式。

items.example: The same root appears in military vocabulary.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根也出现在军事词汇中。

definition_zh: vt. 使暴怒；激怒；使发狂
definition_en: to make someone extremely angry, or to drive an animal into a violent fury
core_image: 一句嘲讽之后，握杯的手先把杯子放下，再抬起来按住桌沿
scene: 一句嘲讽之后，握杯的手先把杯子放下，再抬起来按住桌沿。 One careless remark enrages even the most patient negotiator.
sceneCN: 这里 enrages 指「使暴怒」（第 1 个义项：把人放进怒气里）；句意是一句不经心的话就能让最有耐心的谈判者当场发作。

pos.zh: 使暴怒；激怒；使（动物）发狂

senses.title: To make furiously angry
senses.definition: to make someone extremely angry
senses.definitionCN: （动词）使某人极度愤怒
senses.example: One careless remark enrages even the most patient negotiator.
senses.exampleCN: 一句不经心的话，能让最有耐心的谈判者也当场发作。
senses.why: A coffee cup set down carefully, then a hand flattening the table edge
senses.whyCN: 一只咖啡杯被小心放下，接着一只手按平桌沿

senses.title: To drive an animal to fury
senses.definition: to drive an animal into a violent fury
senses.definitionCN: （动词）使动物陷入狂暴
senses.example: The dogs barked up the slope and enraged the bull.
senses.exampleCN: 狗群沿坡狂吠，把那头公牛激得发狂。
senses.why: A bull stamping the same spot until the dust rises
senses.whyCN: 公牛在同一处反复践踏，尘土扬了起来

senses.title: To provoke on purpose
senses.definition: to provoke anger deliberately
senses.definitionCN: （动词）蓄意激起愤怒
senses.example: The last line was written to enrage the editor.
senses.exampleCN: 最后那一行就是为了让编辑发怒才写下的。
senses.why: One sentence added at the bottom of an otherwise polite letter
senses.whyCN: 一封原本客气的信，末尾多出来的一句话

intro.en: Enrage is en- plus rage. Rage reaches English through Old French from Latin rabere, to be mad, so enrage literally means to put someone inside that madness.
intro.cn: enrage 由 en- 加 rage 构成。rage 经古法语来自拉丁语 rabere（发疯），所以 enrage 的字面意思就是把某人放进那种疯狂里。

items.en: Rabere means to be mad in Latin.
items.cn: 拉丁语 rabere 意为发疯。

items.en: Rabies names the madness passed on by a bite.
items.cn: rabies 指由咬伤传出的疯狂。

items.en: Old French rage carries the noun into French.
items.cn: 古法语 rage 把名词带入法语。

items.en: Rage enters English for violent anger.
items.cn: 13 世纪 rage 进入英语，指暴怒。

items.en: The prefixed verb appears in English writing.
items.cn: 16 世纪带前缀的动词出现在英语书写中。

items.en: Hunting writers apply it to a cornered animal.
items.cn: 17 世纪狩猎写作者把它用于被逼入绝境的动物。

note.en: Enrage and engage differ by one letter; rage and derange share the Latin stem for madness, while infuriate and incense state the same effect from other roots.
note.cn: enrage 与 engage 只差一个字母；rage 与 derange 共用表示疯狂的拉丁词根，而 infuriate 与 incense 从别的词根说明同一种效果。

entries.definition: violent and uncontrollable anger
entries.definitionCN: 暴怒；狂怒

entries.definition: to disturb the order of a mind
entries.definitionCN: 使扰乱；使发疯

entries.definition: to occupy attention or to hire
entries.definitionCN: 使参与；雇用

entries.definition: to make someone extremely angry
entries.definitionCN: 使暴怒；使狂怒

entries.definition: to make someone feel angry
entries.definitionCN: 使生气

entries.definition: to make someone very angry in formal use
entries.definitionCN: 激怒；触怒

entries.definition: to cause anger on purpose or by carelessness
entries.definitionCN: 激起；挑动

normalIntro.en: En plus rage: to put anger into someone
normalIntro.cn: en- 加 rage：把怒气放进一个人身上

normal.en: Rabere is to be mad, rage is the noun it left behind
normal.cn: rabere 是发疯，rage 是它留下的名词

normal.en: En- turns the noun into an act done to someone else
normal.cn: en- 把名词变成对别人做出的动作

normal.en: A cup set down, a hand on the table, a bull in one spot
normal.cn: 一只放下的杯子、按在桌沿的手、原地踏土的公牛

normal.en: Engage and enrage differ by one letter and a great deal of heat
normal.cn: 两个词只差一个字母，火气却差一大截

normal.en: The passive reads most often: the crowd was enraged
normal.cn: 被动式最常见：人群被激怒了

abstract.en: A coffee cup set down carefully, then a hand flattening the table edge
abstract.cn: 一只咖啡杯被小心放下，接着一只手按平桌沿

abstract.en: A bull stamping the same spot until the dust rises
abstract.cn: 公牛在同一处反复践踏，尘土扬了起来

abstract.en: One sentence added at the bottom of an otherwise polite letter
abstract.cn: 一封原本客气的信，末尾多出来的一句话

examples.en: The notice enraged the tenants along the whole street.
examples.cn: 这则通知激怒了整条街的租客。

examples.en: Nothing enraged the driver more than a polite smile.
examples.cn: 没有什么比一个客气的微笑更让那名司机恼怒。

examples.en: The smell of smoke enraged the herd.
examples.cn: 烟味把牛群激得狂躁不安。

dict_mnemonic.text: enrage ＝ en-（使…进入）＋ rage（暴怒）＝「使暴怒」。rage 来自拉丁语 rabere（发疯），同源的 rabies 是狂犬病。前缀 en- 把名词变成及物动词，宾语只能是人或动物。三条线：日常语境使人发火、狩猎语境使动物发狂、写作语境指蓄意挑衅。被动 be enraged 比主动更常用，过去分词 enraged 常作表语或定语。

root: 拉丁语 rabere（发疯）→ 古法语 rage（暴怒）→ en- ＋ rage → enrage（使进入暴怒）

sensesIntro.en: Three heats of anger: a hand on the table edge, a bull in the dust, one extra sentence in a polite letter
sensesIntro.cn: 三种热度不同的怒气：按在桌沿的手、尘土里的公牛、一封客气信里多出来的一句

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup set down first, then a hand pressed flat on the table edge
core.cn: 核心意象：先把杯子放下，随后一只手按平在桌沿

branches.en: A person loses patience.
branches.cn: 一个人失去耐心。

branches.en: An animal loses control.
branches.cn: 一只动物失去控制。

branches.en: Someone plans the provocation.
branches.cn: 有人蓄意挑起。

branches.en: Both begin with words.
branches.cn: 两者都由话语引起。

branches.en: Both end in the body, not in speech.
branches.cn: 两者最后都落在身体上，而不是言语上。

intro.en: Enrage is en- plus rage; en- makes the noun transitive, and rage traces back to Latin rabere, to be mad.
intro.cn: enrage 由 en- 加 rage 构成；en- 使名词变成及物动词，rage 可追溯到拉丁语 rabere（发疯）。

latinIntro.en: Rabere gave Latin rabies and, through Old French, English rage; the same stem returns later in rabid and in derange.
latinIntro.cn: rabere 给出拉丁语 rabies，并经古法语给出英语 rage；同一词根后来在 rabid 与 derange 中再次出现。

definition_zh: 犯罪性；犯罪倾向；犯罪状况（不可数）
definition_en: the quality or state of being criminal, or the extent of crime in a place or a group
core_image: 一张城市地图上，几个街区被红笔圈出，旁边写着案件数量
scene: 研究者在社区中心展示一张标满红点的地图，说明不同街区的案件分布。 Researchers measured criminality by district rather than by city.
sceneCN: 这里 criminality 指某地的犯罪状况（第 1 个义项：犯罪的性质与程度）；句意为研究者按街区而非整座城市衡量犯罪状况。图中可辨识物件：地图、红点、统计表、投影幕。

pos.zh: 犯罪性；犯罪倾向（不可数）
犯罪状况；犯罪程度（社会学用语）

senses.title: The quality of being criminal
senses.titleCN: 犯罪的性质与程度（总称）
senses.definition: the quality or degree of being criminal, considered in the abstract
senses.definitionCN: 抽象地看待「属于犯罪」这一性质及其程度
senses.example: Researchers measured criminality by district rather than by city.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者按街区而非整座城市衡量犯罪状况。
senses.why: Criminal plus -ity makes a quality noun, the abstract counterpart of the adjective.
senses.whyCN: criminal 加 -ity 构成性质名词，是形容词的抽象对应形式。

senses.title: Crime levels in a place
senses.titleCN: 某地或某时期的犯罪状况
senses.definition: the level of offending recorded in a place or period
senses.definitionCN: 某地或某时期记录到的违法水平
senses.example: Criminality in the port rose after the patrols were cut.
senses.exampleCN: 巡逻削减后，港区的犯罪状况恶化。
senses.why: Sociology turned the quality into a measurable state of a place.
senses.whyCN: 社会学把这一性质变成某地可测量的状态。

senses.title: Legal quality of an act
senses.titleCN: 行为在法律上构成犯罪的属性
senses.definition: the character that makes an act punishable under criminal law
senses.definitionCN: 使某项行为在刑法下可受处罚的性质
senses.example: The court examined the criminality of the conduct, not its motive.
senses.exampleCN: 法院审查的是该行为是否构成犯罪，而不是其动机。
senses.why: In law the word names an attribute of conduct, which is why it appears in judgments about whether a charge can be brought.
senses.whyCN: 在法律上这个词指行为的属性，因此常见于判断能否提起指控的判决中。

senses.title: Organised criminality
senses.definition: the scale of coordinated illegal activity in a region or an industry
senses.definitionCN: 某地区或某行业中协同违法活动的规模
senses.example: Criminality in the freight business was organised around two families.
senses.exampleCN: 货运业的犯罪活动围绕两个家族组织起来。
senses.why: Coordination gives crime a size and a structure, and the quality noun measures that structure.
senses.whyCN: 协同让犯罪有了规模与结构，这个性质名词衡量的正是那种结构。

senses.title: The object of criminology
senses.definition: the subject matter that criminology measures, explains and compares
senses.definitionCN: 犯罪学所测量、解释与比较的对象
senses.example: The journal treats criminality as a social process rather than a trait.
senses.exampleCN: 这份期刊把犯罪现象当作社会过程，而不是个人特质。
senses.why: A discipline needs a name for what it measures, and the abstract noun supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 一门学科需要为它所测量的东西命名，这个抽象名词正好提供。

senses.title: A tendency in a person
senses.definition: an individual disposition toward committing offences
senses.definitionCN: 个人实施违法行为的倾向
senses.example: Early writers linked criminality to the shape of the skull.
senses.exampleCN: 早期作者把犯罪倾向与颅骨形状联系起来。
senses.why: Psychology and early criminology used the noun for a trait inside a person.
senses.whyCN: 心理学与早期犯罪学用这个名词指人身上的某种特质。

senses.title: Crime at the level of a state
senses.titleCN: 国家或制度层面的犯罪行为
senses.definition: offending carried out or tolerated by state institutions
senses.definitionCN: 由国家机构实施或纵容的违法行为
senses.example: Scholars of state criminality study deportation and detention records.
senses.exampleCN: 研究国家犯罪的学者考察驱逐与拘留记录。
senses.why: If institutions can act like offenders, the same quality noun can be predicated of a state.
senses.whyCN: 如果机构能像犯罪者一样行动，同一个性质名词就可以用来陈述国家。

senses.title: Contrast with civil wrongs
senses.titleCN: 与民事不法相对的刑事性质
senses.definition: the criminal character that distinguishes an act from a civil wrong
senses.definitionCN: 区分刑事行为与民事侵权的性质
senses.example: The criminality of the act did not remove the victim's right to sue.
senses.exampleCN: 该行为构成犯罪，并不取消受害人起诉的权利。
senses.why: The boundary with civil wrongs is a boundary of character, so the noun names the character itself.
senses.whyCN: 与民事不法的界线是性质的界线，因此这个名词命名的正是那种性质。

intro.en: Criminality is an English formation from criminal plus the noun suffix -ity, which goes back to Latin -itas. Criminal itself comes from Latin criminalis, from crimen 'charge, accusation'. The noun is recorded from the seventeenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: criminality 是在英语内部由 criminal 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，-ity 可上溯至拉丁 -itas。criminal 本身来自拉丁 criminalis，词根为 crimen「指控、控告」。这个名词十七世纪起有记录。年代均为约数。

items.en: Crimen named a charge before it named the deed, and its stem crimin- underlies the family.
items.cn: crimen 先指指控，后指行为，其词干 crimin- 支撑整个词族。

items.en: Criminalis meant 'of a charge, of an offence', and English criminal came from it.
items.cn: criminalis 意为「与指控、罪行有关的」，英语 criminal 由此而来。

items.en: -itas formed abstract quality nouns, the ancestor of English -ity.
items.cn: -itas 构成抽象性质名词，是英语 -ity 的前身。

items.en: English writers built criminality to name the state of being criminal, first in moral and legal argument.
items.cn: 英语作者构造 criminality 来指「属于犯罪的状态」，最初用于道德与法律论辩。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the noun became a technical measure of offending in a population.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个名词成为衡量人群违法状况的技术指标。

items.en: The formation criminal plus -ity is transparent and the chain is clear; only the earliest English citation is not firmly dated.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：criminal 加 -ity 的构成一目了然，词源链清楚，只有英语最早书证没有确定年代。

note.en: Group one holds the crimen family and one look-alike; group two holds terms for the measured side of crime.
note.cn: 第一组是 crimen 词族与一个形近词；第二组是犯罪「可测量一面」的相关术语。

entries.definition: The adjective and the person; criminality is the abstract quality, not the person.
entries.definitionCN: 指形容词或犯罪的人；criminality 是抽象性质，不指人。

entries.definition: The discipline that studies criminality; the two words are often used as if interchangeable but are not.
entries.definitionCN: 研究犯罪性的学科；两者常被当作可互换，其实不同。

entries.definition: To put a charge on someone, not to describe the level of crime.
entries.definitionCN: 把指控加到某人身上，而不是描述犯罪水平。

entries.definition: From discernere 'to separate': to distinguish, unrelated to crimen.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 discernere「分辨」：区分事物，与 crimen 无关。

entries.definition: Offending by young people, from Latin delinquere 'to fail'; narrower in age than criminality.
entries.definitionCN: 青少年的违法行为，出自拉丁 delinquere「失职」；在年龄范围上比 criminality 更窄。

entries.definition: Behaviour that departs from social norms, only some of which is criminal.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离社会规范的行为，其中只有一部分构成犯罪。

entries.definition: A condition in which law is not enforced, wider than the rate of offences.
entries.definitionCN: 法律得不到执行的状况，比犯罪率更宽泛。

entries.definition: Bad conduct in general, with no statistical sense at all.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指不良行为，完全不含统计意味。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Criminal plus -ity: the state of being criminal, treated as a quantity.
normal.cn: criminal 加 -ity：把「属于犯罪」的状态当作一个量来看。

normal.en: The family runs crime, criminal, criminality, criminalize, criminology.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 crime、criminal、criminality、criminalize 与 criminology。

normal.en: Sociology pairs it with rates and causes: rates of criminality, root causes of criminality.
normal.cn: 社会学常与比率和成因搭配：犯罪率、犯罪根源。

normal.en: The word is uncountable: one speaks of criminality, not of a criminality.
normal.cn: 这个词不可数：说 criminality，而不说 a criminality。

normal.en: Criminology studies criminality; the two words are related but not synonyms.
normal.cn: 犯罪学研究 criminality；两者相关，但不是同义词。

abstract.en: Picture a map with certain blocks shaded darker than the rest.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，某些街区被涂得比别处更暗。

abstract.en: Picture a quality that can be poured into a chart and read as a curve.
abstract.cn: 想象一种性质被倒进图表，读出来是一条曲线。

abstract.en: Picture a word that turns a person's act into a property of a whole district.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词把个人的行为变成整个街区的属性。

examples.en: Comparative criminality is hard to measure when reporting habits differ.
examples.cn: 当各地的报案习惯不同时，犯罪状况很难比较衡量。

examples.en: The report traced juvenile criminality to school exclusion.
examples.cn: 报告把青少年犯罪追溯到被学校排除这一原因。

examples.en: They argued that the criminality of the act depends on the wording of the statute.
examples.cn: 他们主张该行为是否构成犯罪取决于法条的措辞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「criminal（犯罪的）+ ity（性质）」——犯罪的性质与程度

root: 英语 criminal（拉丁 criminalis，词根 crimen「指控、罪行」）+ 名词后缀 -ity（拉丁 -itas，表性质）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from an abstract quality to a measured place, then to a legal attribute, an organised scale, a research object, a personal tendency, a state practice and a contrast with civil wrongs.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从抽象性质走向可测量的地区，再到法律属性、有组织规模、研究对象、个人倾向、国家行为，以及与民事不法的对照。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a city map with certain blocks ringed in red and case numbers written beside them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张城市地图，几个街区被红笔圈出，旁边写着案件数量。

branches.en: THE QUALITY AND ITS AMOUNT: first an abstract property, then a level recorded in a place.
branches.cn: 性质与数量：先是抽象属性，再是某地记录到的水平。

branches.en: THE LEGAL TEST: the word names what makes conduct punishable, regardless of motive.
branches.cn: 法律判断：这个名词指使行为可受刑罚的性质，与动机无关。

branches.en: SCALE AND STUDY: coordinated activity has a size, and a discipline takes that size as its object.
branches.cn: 规模与研究：协同活动有大小，而一门学科把这一大小当作研究对象。

branches.en: INSIDE A PERSON: psychology reads the noun as a disposition or trait.
branches.cn: 一个人之内：心理学把这个名词读成倾向或特质。

branches.en: THE STATE AND THE CIVIL LINE: institutions can offend, and the criminal character marks a boundary against civil wrongs.
branches.cn: 国家与民事界线：机构也会违法，而刑事性质划出了与民事侵权的界线。

intro.en: Criminality joins a Latin-derived adjective to a Latin-derived suffix inside English.
intro.cn: criminality 在英语内部把一个拉丁来源的形容词与一个拉丁来源的后缀接在一起。

latinIntro.en: Crimen gives criminal and its relatives; -itas supplies the abstract ending that becomes -ity.
latinIntro.cn: crimen 衍生 criminal 及其同族词；-itas 提供抽象词尾，后演变为 -ity。

items.example: The stem carries the legal idea.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干承载法律含义。

items.example: The criminal court sat on Monday.
items.exampleCN: 刑事法院周一开庭。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into a quality noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成性质名词。

items.meaning: the state or extent of crime
items.example: Criminality was mapped by ward.
items.exampleCN: 犯罪状况按选区绘制成图。

items.example: The criminal was released in spring.
items.exampleCN: 这名罪犯在春天获释。

items.meaning: in a criminal way; to a criminal degree
items.example: The files were criminally neglected.
items.exampleCN: 这些档案被严重疏忽，几近犯罪。

items.example: The law criminalized the practice.
items.exampleCN: 法律把这种做法定为犯罪。

items.example: Criminology measures what courts record.
items.exampleCN: 犯罪学测量法院记录下来的东西。

definition_zh: 遗忘症；失忆；记忆缺失
definition_en: partial or total loss of memory, especially from illness, injury, or shock
core_image: 被橡皮擦擦掉的记事本：过去的页面突然一片空白
scene: 车祸醒来后，他连自己的名字都说不出来。 The accident left him with temporary amnesia.
sceneCN: 这里的 amnesia 是「失忆症」（第 1 个义项：因伤病导致的记忆丧失）；句意是这场事故让他患上了暂时性失忆。

pos.zh: 失忆症；记忆丧失

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀 -ac 构成，义为「失忆症患者」；亦可作形容词「失忆的」
加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，义为「失忆的；引起失忆的」

senses.title: Loss of memory caused by injury or illness
senses.titleCN: 病理性失忆：伤病造成的记忆丧失
senses.definition: the medical condition of losing memories, wholly or partly, because of brain injury or disease
senses.definitionCN: 因脑损伤或疾病而全部或部分丧失记忆的病症
senses.example: The boxer's amnesia erased the night of the fight.
senses.exampleCN: 这位拳手的失忆抹去了比赛当晚的记忆。
senses.why: The Greek root mnasthai means to remember, and the prefix a- cancels it outright.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语词根 mnasthai 意为「记得」，否定前缀 a- 直接将其取消。

senses.title: Inability to form new memories
senses.titleCN: 顺行性失忆：无法形成新记忆
senses.definition: the condition of being unable to retain new information after an event
senses.definitionCN: 某事件之后无法留存新信息的状态
senses.example: After the surgery he developed anterograde amnesia.
senses.exampleCN: 手术后他患上了顺行性失忆。
senses.why: Medicine split the blank page in two: nothing before, or nothing after.
senses.whyCN: 医学把「空白页」一分为二：之前记不住，或之后存不进。

senses.title: Loss of memories from before an event
senses.titleCN: 逆行性失忆：忘记事发之前的往事
senses.definition: loss of memories acquired before the injury or onset of illness
senses.definitionCN: 丧失受伤或发病之前获得的记忆
senses.example: Retrograde amnesia took away her wedding day.
senses.exampleCN: 逆行性失忆带走了她婚礼那天的记忆。
senses.why: The erased page is behind the patient; the past is what vanishes.
senses.whyCN: 被擦掉的页码在患者身后——消失的是过去。

senses.title: Psychologically motivated forgetting
senses.titleCN: 心因性遗忘：因心理冲击而忘却
senses.definition: memory loss attributed to emotional trauma rather than physical damage
senses.definitionCN: 归因于情感创伤而非躯体损伤的记忆丧失
senses.example: His amnesia about the crash was the mind's shield.
senses.exampleCN: 他对车祸的失忆是心灵自我保护的盾牌。
senses.why: The mind can also reach for the eraser when remembering hurts too much.
senses.whyCN: 当回忆过于痛苦，心灵也会主动拿起橡皮擦。

senses.title: Figurative forgetting by a group or public
senses.titleCN: 集体失忆：群体对往事的遗忘
senses.definition: a society's or group's failure to remember its own past
senses.definitionCN: 社会或群体对自身历史的遗忘
senses.example: The town's collective amnesia hid the factory disaster from memory.
senses.exampleCN: 小镇的集体失忆让工厂事故从记忆中消失。
senses.why: What an individual brain does, a culture can do too, metaphorically.
senses.whyCN: 个体大脑会发生的事，文化在隐喻上同样会发生。

senses.title: Convenient forgetting of duty or facts
senses.titleCN: 选择性健忘：对义务事实的装忘
senses.definition: informal forgetfulness about obligations or inconvenient facts, as if deliberate
senses.definitionCN: 对义务或不便事实的健忘，仿佛有意为之
senses.example: The agency suffers amnesia every audit season.
senses.exampleCN: 每到审计季，这个机构就「失忆」。
senses.why: Speakers borrowed the medical term to accuse others of convenient forgetting.
senses.whyCN: 人们借医学术语来指责他人「 conveniently 忘记」该记得的事。

intro.en: Amnesia is a Greek coinage: the prefix a- (not) plus mnasthai (to remember), later applied to memory loss.
intro.cn: amnesia 是希腊语造词：前缀 a-（不）加 mnasthai（记得），后被用于指记忆丧失。

items.en: Root *men-, to think, also seen in mind and mental.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *men-「思考」，也见于 mind、mental。

items.en: mnasthai, to remember; related to mneme, memory, and Mnemosyne, the memory goddess.
items.cn: 希腊语 mnasthai「记得」，与 mneme（记忆）及记忆女神 Mnemosyne 同族。

items.en: amnesia formed with a- (not) for forgetfulness.
items.cn: 希腊语加否定前缀 a- 构成 amnesia「健忘」。

items.en: amnesia entered medical Latin as a term for loss of memory.
items.cn: amnesia 以「记忆丧失」之意进入新拉丁医学术语。

items.en: English amnesia appears in medical texts around 1700.
items.cn: 约 1700 年前后，英语 amnesia 见于医学文献。

items.en: Now covers clinical syndromes and figurative group or convenient forgetting.
items.cn: 如今既指临床综合征，也用于集体或选择性遗忘的比喻。

note.en: Set amnesia against its memory-root cousins and near words for forgetting.
note.cn: 把 amnesia 与同属「记忆」词根的词以及其他表示遗忘的词区分开。

entries.definition: an official pardon; literally not-remembering a crime — same root, different target.
entries.definitionCN: 大赦；字面即「不再记得罪行」，同根但对象不同，注意区分。

entries.definition: a memory aid; the opposite in meaning, sharing the mn- root.
entries.definitionCN: 记忆辅助物；意义与 amnesia 相反，同属 mn- 词根。

entries.definition: sleeplessness; built like amnesia with a negative prefix plus a Greek noun.
entries.definitionCN: 失眠；构词与 amnesia 平行：否定前缀加希腊名词。

entries.definition: everyday failing to remember, without medical implication.
entries.definitionCN: 日常健忘，不带病理含义。

entries.definition: a span of lost memory, often from alcohol or fainting.
entries.definitionCN: 记忆断片，常因醉酒或晕厥。

entries.definition: progressive cognitive decline of which memory loss is one part.
entries.definitionCN: 渐进性认知衰退，记忆丧失只是其一部分。

normalIntro.en: Use the mn- root family to fix amnesia in memory.
normalIntro.cn: 用 mn- 词根家族把 amnesia 钉在记忆里。

normal.en: a- (not) + mnesia (remember): not-remembering.
normal.cn: a-（不）+ mnesia（记得）：不记得。

normal.en: Same root trio: amnesia (loss), amnesty (pardon), mnemonic (aid).
normal.cn: 同根三兄弟：amnesia（失忆）、amnesty（赦免）、mnemonic（记忆术）。

normal.en: Parallel words: insomnia (not sleeping), anesthesia (not feeling).
normal.cn: 平行词：insomnia（不眠）、anesthesia（无感觉）。

normal.en: Retrograde = backwards before; anterograde = forwards after.
normal.cn: retrograde（逆行）忘的是从前；anterograde（顺行）存不进以后。

normal.en: amnesiac is the patient; amnesic is the adjective.
normal.cn: amnesiac 指患者；amnesic 是形容词。

abstract.en: Picture an eraser sweeping across a diary until the pages are blank.
abstract.cn: 想象橡皮擦扫过日记本，纸页一片空白。

abstract.en: Mnemosyne the memory goddess turns her back, and names vanish.
abstract.cn: 记忆女神 Mnemosyne 转过身去，名字随之消失。

abstract.en: A man holding a suitcase with no label: everything about himself erased.
abstract.cn: 一个拎着无标签行李箱的人：关于自己的一切都被抹去。

examples.en: The novel's hero wakes on a beach with total amnesia.
examples.cn: 小说主人公在海滩上醒来，完全失忆。

examples.en: Doctors tested his memory for signs of amnesia.
examples.cn: 医生检测他的记忆，寻找失忆的迹象。

examples.en: The nation must not fall into amnesia about its darkest chapter.
examples.cn: 这个民族绝不能对最黑暗的一章集体失忆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿姆你谢」——阿姆见到你却鞠躬说「您是哪位」？因为他失忆了，认不出人。

root: 希腊语 a-（不）+ mnasthai（记得，源自印欧词根 *men-「思考」）→ 新拉丁医学用语 amnesia → 英语 amnesia（失忆）。同根词：amnesty（大赦）、mnemonic（记忆术）、Mnemosyne（记忆女神）、mind、mental。

sensesIntro.en: From the clinical blank page, amnesia spreads to trauma-forgotten pasts, new-memory failures, and societies that forget on purpose.
sensesIntro.cn: 从临床的「空白页」出发，amnesia 扩展到创伤遗忘、新记忆障碍，以及群体的选择性遗忘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a diary page wiped blank
core.cn: 核心意象：被擦成空白的日记页

branches.en: Medical memory loss from damage or disease
branches.cn: 损伤疾病导致的病理性记忆丧失

branches.en: Directional syndromes: before or after the event
branches.cn: 方向性综合征：忘前或忘后

branches.en: The mind's protective forgetting
branches.cn: 心灵自我保护的遗忘

branches.en: Societies erasing their own record
branches.cn: 社会抹去自身记忆

branches.en: Individuals conveniently forgetting duties
branches.cn: 个人对义务的装忘

intro.en: Amnesia shows the Greek negative a- joined to a memory root, a pattern copied by many medical terms.
intro.cn: amnesia 体现希腊否定前缀 a- 加「记忆」词根的构词，许多医学术语都仿照这一模式。

latinIntro.en: The same mn- root and a- prefix travel together through Greek-derived vocabulary.
latinIntro.cn: 同样的 mn- 词根与 a- 前缀在希腊源词汇中结伴出现。

items.example: anarchy means without rule
items.exampleCN: anarchy 即「无统治」

items.example: mnemonic devices aid recall
items.exampleCN: 记忆术帮助回忆

items.example: amnesia names a condition
items.exampleCN: amnesia 指一种病症

items.meaningCN: 大赦；对罪行的「不再记得」
items.example: the government declared amnesty
items.exampleCN: 政府宣布大赦

items.example: a mnemonic rhyme for spelling
items.exampleCN: 帮助拼写的记忆口诀

items.meaning: goddess of memory, mother of the Muses
items.example: Mnemosyne inspired ancient poets
items.exampleCN: 记忆女神启发了古代诗人

items.example: coffee worsens her insomnia
items.exampleCN: 咖啡加重她的失眠

items.example: the operation needs anesthesia
items.exampleCN: 手术需要麻醉

items.example: care for dementia patients
items.exampleCN: 照护痴呆患者

items.example: retrograde amnesia erases the past
items.exampleCN: 逆行性失忆抹去过去

definition_zh: 政府的；政府性质的；由政府作出的；与政府层级或政府行为方式有关的
definition_en: relating to a government as an institution, or characteristic of the way governments act
core_image: 办事大厅里，窗口前的人递上表格，工作人员逐份盖章，墙上贴着刚换的新规
scene: 办事大厅里，窗口前的人递上表格，工作人员逐份盖章，墙上贴着刚换的新规。 The new rule came from a governmental body, not from the court.
sceneCN: 这里指「由政府机构作出的」，对应第 2 个义项：属于政府机关这一类的；句意为这条新规出自一个政府机构，而不是法院。画面要点：办事窗口、成叠表格、墙上的规章。

pos.zh: 政府的；与政府机构有关的
政府式的；带有官僚作风的（含贬义时）

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

derivatives.zh: 州长的；与州长职位有关的

senses.title: Relating to government as an institution
senses.titleCN: 与作为机构的政府有关
senses.definition: concerned with the bodies that hold public authority in a state
senses.definitionCN: 涉及在一国中掌握公共权威的那些机构
senses.example: The report described the governmental structure of the new federation.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告描述了新联邦的政府结构。
senses.why: the adjective is simply the noun for government plus the usual relational ending, so it marks belonging to the institution.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是「政府」这一名词加常见的关联词尾，因此它标记的是归属于该机构。

senses.title: Describing an official body or agency
senses.titleCN: 形容属于政府机关这一类
senses.definition: used of an organisation that acts under state authority rather than as a private party
senses.definitionCN: 用于按国家权威、而非以私人身份行事的组织
senses.example: The new rule came from a governmental body, not from the court.
senses.exampleCN: 这条新规出自一个政府机构，而不是法院。
senses.why: organisations need to be sorted by whose authority they act under, and the adjective marks the public side of that line.
senses.whyCN: 组织需要按「依谁的权威行事」来分类，这个形容词标记的就是这条界线的公家一侧。

senses.title: Issued as policy or regulation
senses.titleCN: 由政府作为政策或规章发布
senses.definition: describing rules, standards or programmes that carry the force of state decision
senses.definitionCN: 形容具有国家决定效力的规则、标准或计划
senses.example: Governmental regulation of the port slowed every shipment.
senses.exampleCN: 政府对港口的规章让每一批货都慢了下来。
senses.why: an institution acts through documents, so the adjective attaches to the instruments it issues.
senses.whyCN: 机构是通过文件行动的，因此这个形容词也附着在它所发布的文书上。

senses.title: Funded or owned by the state
senses.definition: describing money, property or staff supplied from public funds
senses.definitionCN: 形容由公共资金提供的款项、财产或人员
senses.example: The clinic survived on governmental funding for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所靠政府拨款撑了十年。
senses.why: once government is an institution, its purse becomes a source, and the adjective names that source.
senses.whyCN: 政府一旦是机构，其钱袋就成了一个来源，这个形容词便用来指那个来源。

senses.title: Belonging to a level of government
senses.definition: used to place a decision at the local, regional or national rung of the system
senses.definitionCN: 用于把某项决定放在地方、区域或国家某一级上
senses.example: The dispute had to be settled at the governmental level, not in a workshop.
senses.exampleCN: 这场争端必须在政府层面解决，而不能在车间里解决。
senses.why: states are layered, so the adjective works with level words to say which layer is speaking.
senses.whyCN: 国家是分层的，因此这个形容词与「层级」一类词连用，说明是哪一层在说话。

senses.title: Behaving in a bureaucratic way
senses.definition: describing slow, form-bound behaviour that resembles the worst habits of public offices
senses.definitionCN: 形容缓慢、拘于表格、类似公署最坏习气的行为
senses.example: The approval process was painfully governmental.
senses.exampleCN: 这套审批流程慢得像政府办事一样。
senses.why: a word for belonging to an institution can also criticise the manner of that institution, and the tone turns negative.
senses.whyCN: 一个表示归属机构的词，也能用来批评该机构的行事方式，此时语气转为贬义。

senses.title: Derived from state authority
senses.definition: describing a power, right or appointment whose force comes from the state rather than from contract
senses.definitionCN: 形容某项权力、权利或任命的力量来自国家，而非来自合同
senses.example: A governmental power of entry does not need the owner's consent.
senses.exampleCN: 政府的进入权不需要业主同意。
senses.why: authority has sources, and this adjective marks the one that traces back to the state rather than to agreement.
senses.whyCN: 权威有其来源，这个形容词标记的是可追溯到国家、而非追溯到约定的那一种。

senses.title: Abstract: pertaining to steering a community
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：关乎如何驾驭一个共同体
senses.definition: in general use, concerning the direction of any collective body, not only a state
senses.definitionCN: 泛指关乎任何集体如何被引导，而不限于国家
senses.example: A university has its own governmental problems.
senses.exampleCN: 一所大学也有它自己的治理难题。
senses.why: the base verb means to steer, so the adjective can be read as 'having to do with steering', at any scale.
senses.whyCN: 基础动词意为「掌舵」，因此这个形容词可读作「与掌舵有关的」，在任何规模上都成立。

intro.en: Governmental is government plus a relational adjective ending, and government goes back through French to a Latin verb borrowed from Greek for steering a ship. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: governmental 是 government 加关系形容词词尾构成，而 government 经法语上溯到一个借自希腊语、本义为「掌舵」的拉丁动词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Kybernan meant 'to steer, pilot a ship', and kybernetes meant the steersman; the deeper origin of the Greek verb is not established, so any older root offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: kybernan 意为「掌舵、驾驶船只」，kybernetes 指舵手；这个希腊动词更深的来源未得到证明，凡为其提出的更早词根均属重构形式。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek verb as gubernare 'to steer, pilot, direct', and from it came gubernator 'steersman' and gubernaculum 'rudder'.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个希腊动词借作 gubernare「掌舵、驾驶、指引」，由它产生 gubernator「舵手」与 gubernaculum「船舵」。

items.en: Old French governer carried the verb into English in the fourteenth century, where govern first meant to steer or guide and soon also to rule.
items.cn: 古法语 governer 在十四世纪把这个动词带入英语，govern 最初指掌舵、引导，随后也指统治。

items.en: Government was formed in the fourteenth century from govern plus the noun ending -ment; it first named the act of governing and later the body that governs.
items.cn: government 于十四世纪由 govern 加构成名词的词尾构成；最初指治理这一行为，后来指治理的机构。

items.en: The adjective governmental, formed with the relational ending -al, spread in the nineteenth century as administrative writing needed a word for what belongs to government rather than to the governed.
items.cn: 形容词 governmental 由表示「与……相关」的关系词尾构成，在十九世纪随行政文书的增长而普及，因为那时需要一个词来指属于政府、而非属于被治理者的事物。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Greek root of kybernan is disputed, and the earliest use of the English adjective is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：kybernan 在希腊语之前的词根存在争议，这个英语形容词的最早用例只能给出约略年代。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same steering stem that are easily confused with this adjective; group two holds adjectives that also describe public authority.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「掌舵」词干、容易与本词混淆的形式；第二组是同样描述公共权威的形容词。

entries.definition: The institution or the act of governing; the adjective describes what belongs to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指机构或治理行为；本词形容词描述属于它的事物。

entries.definition: The way decisions are made and supervised, often in firms and agencies; it names a process, not a belonging.
entries.definitionCN: 指决定如何作出与监督的方式，常用于企业与机构；它指过程，而非归属。

entries.definition: Relating to the office of a state governor; the stem is the same but the reference is to one post, not to government as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 与州长职位有关；词干相同，但所指是一个职位，而非整个政府。

entries.definition: Describing the body or party that is in power now, as a governing party; it marks present activity, not institutional type.
entries.definitionCN: 形容目前执政的机构或政党，如执政党；它标记当下的活动，而非机构类型。

entries.definition: Approved by a body with authority, which may be a club or a federation; governmental always points to the state.
entries.definitionCN: 经有权威的机构认可，该机构可能是社团或联合会；而 governmental 总是指向国家。

entries.definition: Operated by the state itself, as a state-run railway; governmental can describe policy without direct operation.
entries.definitionCN: 由国家直接运营，如国营铁路；governmental 可仅描述政策，不涉及直接运营。

entries.tag: the whole economy of the state
entries.definition: Relating to the part of the economy owned or paid for by the state; it is an economic category rather than a legal one.
entries.definitionCN: 与由国家所有或支付的那部分经济有关；属经济范畴，而非法律范畴。

entries.definition: Relating to the running of an organisation; an administrative decision may be internal and carry no public authority.
entries.definitionCN: 与机构的日常管理有关；行政决定可能是内部的，不具公共权威。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The base verb meant to steer a ship, so governing is steering and the adjective marks what belongs to the steersman.
normal.cn: 基础动词意为掌舵，所以治理就是掌舵，而这个形容词标记属于舵手的事物。

normal.en: The family runs govern, government, governor, governance and gubernatorial.
normal.cn: 同族词包括治理、政府、州长、治理方式与州长的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the main uses: governmental body, governmental policy, governmental funding.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示主要用法：政府机构、政府政策、政府拨款。

normal.en: The word entered English through French, and its relative gubernatorial came more directly from Latin.
normal.cn: 这个词经法语进入英语，而同族的「州长的」则更直接地来自拉丁语。

normal.en: Its opposite side is the governed, those on whom authority is exercised.
normal.cn: 它的对面是被治理者，即权威施于其上的那些人。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a rudder while a whole crew waits for the course to be set.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手扶着舵，整船人等着航线被定下。

abstract.en: Picture a counter with a rubber stamp, and a queue that moves one form at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一个放着印章的柜台，队伍一次只前进一份表格。

abstract.en: Picture a building with many floors, each claiming the right to decide the same question.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋很多层的楼，每层都声称有权决定同一个问题。

examples.en: The agency was created by governmental decision, not by treaty.
examples.cn: 这个机构是依政府的决定设立的，而不是依条约。

examples.en: Governmental support kept the archive open through the winter.
examples.cn: 政府的支持让档案馆熬过了整个冬天。

examples.en: The review found the response slow and overly governmental.
examples.cn: 评估认为这次应对迟缓，官僚气过重。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「掌舵 + 名词 + 形容词」——凡属于掌舵那一套机构的事 → 政府的

root: governmental 由 government 加关系形容词词尾构成；government 出自 govern 加名词词尾，govern 经古法语出自拉丁 gubernare「掌舵、指引」，而该拉丁动词借自希腊 kybernan「掌舵」，更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses spread from one institution: what belongs to government, what counts as a public body, what it issues, what it funds, which layer acts, how it behaves, where its authority comes from, and finally any steering of a group.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项由一个机构向外铺开：属于政府的事物、算作公共机构的组织、它发布的文书、它出的钱、由哪一层出面、它的行事作风、它权威的来源，最后是任何对群体的驾驭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stamp coming down on a form at a public counter.
core.cn: 核心意象：公章在办事窗口的一份表格上落下去。

branches.en: INSTITUTION: the adjective first marks what belongs to the body that holds public authority.
branches.cn: 机构：这个形容词首先标记属于掌握公共权威的那个机构的事物。

branches.en: BODY AND INSTRUMENT: an agency is sorted as public, and the rules it issues carry that same mark.
branches.cn: 机关与文书：一个机构被划为公家，它发布的规则也带着同一个印记。

branches.en: MONEY AND LAYER: the state pays for things and also speaks at a particular rung of the system.
branches.cn: 钱与层级：国家既出钱办事，也在体系的某一级上说话。

branches.en: MANNER AND SOURCE: the same adjective can mock bureaucratic slowness or trace a power back to the state.
branches.cn: 作风与来源：同一个形容词既能嘲讽官僚式的迟缓，也能把某项权力追溯至国家。

branches.en: STEERING: the ship image returns, and the adjective applies to any group being guided.
branches.cn: 掌舵：船的画面回来了，这个形容词可用于任何被引导的群体。

intro.en: Governmental is a noun of action plus a relational ending, and the noun rests on a verb that came into Latin from Greek seamanship.
intro.cn: governmental 是行为名词加关系词尾，而这个名词立在一个由希腊航海用语进入拉丁语的动词上。

latinIntro.en: Latin gubernare and gubernator supply govern, governor, government and gubernatorial, all through the image of a rudder.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 gubernare 与 gubernator 衍生出治理、州长、政府与州长的，全都围绕船舵这一意象。

items.example: The Greek verb supplies the image of a hand on the rudder.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊动词提供「手握船舵」的意象。

items.structure: gubernare (Latin verb, first conjugation, from Greek)
items.example: The Latin verb widened from ships to states.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词从船只扩用到国家。

items.example: The agent noun later named a provincial ruler.
items.exampleCN: 这个表人名词后来指一方长官。

items.structure: Old French governer, from Latin gubernare
items.example: To govern is first to set a course.
items.exampleCN: 治理首先是定下航线。

items.example: The ending first named the act of steering.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾最初指掌舵这一行为。

items.example: The noun moved from action to institution.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词从行为转指机构。

items.example: The ending marks what belongs to the institution.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记属于该机构的事物。

items.example: The governor of a province answers to the centre.
items.exampleCN: 一省的长官向中央负责。

items.example: Good governance is measured by how decisions are reviewed.
items.exampleCN: 良好治理要看决定如何被复核。

latinEntries.structure: gubernare, gubernavi, gubernatum (verb, first conjugation; from Greek)

definition_zh: 属；（生物分类的）属；逻辑上的属；一类
definition_en: a rank in biological classification above species and below family, or a class that contains subordinate kinds
core_image: 同一排标本盒里装着几种相似的动物，盒盖写着它们共用的名称
scene: 同一属里的几种猫科动物被排在同一排标本盒中，盒盖上写着它们共用的名称。 Several cat species of the same genus are arranged in one row of specimen boxes, with their shared name written on the lids.
sceneCN: 这里 genus 是「属」（第 1 个义项：位于种之上、科之下的分类阶元）；句意：同一属里的几种猫科动物被排在同一排标本盒中，盒盖上写着它们共用的名称。

pos.zh: 属（复数 genera）；逻辑上的属；一类

senses.title: The rank above species
senses.definition: the taxonomic rank that groups one or more species sharing a common ancestor and a set of structural features
senses.definitionCN: 把共享祖先与一组结构特征的一个或多个物种聚合起来的分类阶元
senses.example: The genus contains four species, two of them recently described.
senses.exampleCN: 这个属包含四个物种，其中两个是最近描述的。
senses.why: Latin genus meant 'birth, race, kind'; taxonomy kept 'kind' and gave it a fixed position: a kind that holds smaller kinds.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 genus 意为「出生、族类、种类」；分类学保留了「种类」义，并给它固定位置：一个装更小种类的种类。

senses.title: The first word of a binomial
senses.definition: the capitalized element placed first in the two-part scientific name of a species
senses.definitionCN: 物种两段式学名中置于最前、首字母大写的成分
senses.example: The genus name is capitalized and may be abbreviated after first use.
senses.exampleCN: 属名首字母大写，首次出现之后可以缩写。
senses.why: A binomial is an address written in two words, and the genus is the street while the species epithet is the house.
senses.whyCN: 双名法是用两个词写成的地址：属名是街道，种加词是门牌。

senses.title: The logical genus containing species
senses.definition: in logic, a wider class that contains narrower classes as its species, the relation of genus and species
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑学中作为种的上位、包含较窄类别的较宽类别，即属与种的关系
senses.example: Animal is the genus and bird the species in the old scheme.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧方案中，动物是属，鸟是种。
senses.why: Logic had the pair before biology: genus and species named containment, and Linnaeus borrowed a ready-made ladder.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学早于生物学拥有这对词：属与种表示包含关系，林奈借用的是一架现成的梯子。

senses.title: A kind or class in general
senses.definition: a broad kind of thing, often in the phrase a genus of, where the reference is not biological
senses.definitionCN: 宽泛的一类事物，常用于 a genus of 结构，所指并非生物
senses.example: A genus of problems resisted every standard method.
senses.exampleCN: 有一类问题抵抗所有标准方法。
senses.why: The everyday sense keeps the Latin breadth: any class that holds smaller classes can be called a genus, with or without specimens.
senses.whyCN: 日常义保留了拉丁语的宽度：任何容纳更小类别的类别都可以叫 genus，与标本无关。

senses.title: The plural genera
senses.definition: the Latin third-declension plural, used in English for several genera and often a marker of technical writing
senses.definitionCN: 拉丁第三变格法复数，英语中用来指多个属，也常成为技术写作的标志
senses.example: Three genera were moved into the new family.
senses.exampleCN: 三个属被移入新科。
senses.why: English keeps genera because the Latin plural is fixed in the codes; using genuses marks a speaker as an outsider.
senses.whyCN: 英语保留 genera，因为法规固定了拉丁复数；说 genuses 会显出外行。

senses.title: The type genus of a family
senses.definition: the genus that gives a family its name and fixes the application of that family name
senses.definitionCN: 为某科提供名称、并固定该科名适用范围的那个属
senses.example: The family takes its name from the type genus.
senses.exampleCN: 这个科的名字取自其模式属。
senses.why: Names must be anchored somewhere, and the type genus is that anchor: the family name is built from it and cannot drift away.
senses.whyCN: 名称必须有锚点，模式属就是那个锚：科名由它构成，因此不能漂移。

senses.title: A monotypic genus
senses.definition: a genus that contains only one species, so the genus and the species carry almost the same content
senses.definitionCN: 只含一个物种的属，属与种的内容因此几乎相同
senses.example: The monotypic genus has no second species to compare with.
senses.exampleCN: 这个单型属没有第二个物种可供比较。
senses.why: When a genus holds one species, the rank above adds no information; taxonomists argue whether such genera should be kept.
senses.whyCN: 当一个属只含一个物种时，上一级并不增加信息；分类学家因此争论这样的属是否应当保留。

senses.title: The adjective generic and its drift
senses.titleCN: 派生形容词 generic 的语义漂移
senses.definition: the derived adjective meaning 'of a genus', which has also come to mean 'common to a whole class' and hence 'unbranded'
senses.definitionCN: 派生形容词，意为「属的」，又引申为「整类共有的」，进而指「无品牌的」
senses.example: Generic names on the shelf told the shopper nothing about the maker.
senses.exampleCN: 货架上的通用名称没有告诉顾客任何关于厂家的事。
senses.why: From 'of a kind' to 'shared by the whole kind' to 'having no distinctive mark': the drift is visible in the word generic, not in genus itself.
senses.whyCN: 从「某一类的」到「整类共有的」再到「没有独特标记的」：这一漂移体现在 generic 一词中，而非 genus 本身。

intro.en: Genus is a Latin noun taken into English with its Latin plural genera. It meant 'birth, origin, race, kind' and became the rank above species. Dates are approximate, and the Indo-European root is reconstructed.
intro.cn: genus 是连同拉丁复数 genera 一起进入英语的拉丁名词，意为「出生、起源、族类、种类」，后来成为物种之上的阶元。年代为约数，印欧词根属重构。

items.en: Genus, generis meant 'birth, descent, race, kind'. It was a third-declension neuter noun and already covered both ancestry and category.
items.cn: genus, generis 意为「出生、血统、族类、种类」，是第三变格法中性名词，本已兼指血统与类别。

items.en: The noun is tied to gignere 'to beget, bring forth', which also gives genius, generate and genital.
items.cn: 该名词与 gignere「生育、产生」相关，后者还给出 genius、generate 与 genital。

items.en: The deeper root is reconstructed as *ǵenh₁- 'to beget', also behind Greek genos and Latin gens; the reconstruction is conventional rather than attested.
items.cn: 更深词根被重构为 *ǵenh₁-「生育」，也见于希腊语 genos 与拉丁 gens；这一重构是通行做法，并非有据可查。

items.en: Before biology, genus named the wider class in the pair genus and species, a relation of containment.
items.cn: 在生物学之前，genus 指属种对中的上位类别，是一种包含关系。

items.en: Linnaeus placed genus immediately above species in the eighteenth century and made its name the first word of the binomial.
items.cn: 林奈在 18 世纪把属置于种之上，并让属名成为双名法的第一个词。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the exact English first use is not fixed here, and the pre-Latin root is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：genus 最早的英语使用此处无法确定；拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates words that look like genus but are not the same noun; group two compares the ranks and relations around it.
note.cn: 第一组区分看似 genus 却并非同一名词的词；第二组比较它周围的阶元与关系。

entries.definition: Inborn talent or a guiding spirit, from Latin genius 'attendant spirit', tied to gignere. It shares the root but is not the taxonomic rank.
entries.definitionCN: 天生的才能或守护神，来自拉丁 genius「守护灵」，与 gignere 相关。它共用词根，但不是分类阶元。

entries.definition: Authentic, from Latin genuinus 'natural, native'. It looks close but does not descend from genus.
entries.definitionCN: 真正的、地道的，来自拉丁 genuinus「天然的、本生的」。外形相近，却不出自 genus。

entries.definition: The Latin plural of genus, required in technical writing. It is the same word in another number, not another concept.
entries.definitionCN: genus 的拉丁复数，技术写作中必须使用。它是同一个词的另一种数，而非另一个概念。

entries.definition: The case of possession, from the same Latin stock but naming a grammatical function rather than a rank.
entries.definitionCN: 表示所属的格，出自同一拉丁词源，却指语法功能而非分类阶元。

entries.definition: The basic rank contained within a genus; the second word of a binomial.
entries.definitionCN: 包含在属之内的基本阶元；双名法的第二个词。

entries.definition: The rank above genus, grouping several genera that share a deeper common ancestry.
entries.definitionCN: 属之上的阶元，把共享更深共同祖先的若干属聚合起来。

entries.definition: Any named group at any rank. A genus is one kind of taxon, not its synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 任一阶元上被命名的类群。属是分类单元的一种，而非其同义词。

entries.definition: The genus that names and fixes a family; it is a role a genus can play, not a separate rank.
entries.definitionCN: 为科命名并固定其范围的那个属；它是属可以担任的角色，不是另一个阶元。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: genus comes from gignere 'to beget': a genus is a kind traced to a common birth.
normal.cn: genus 出自 gignere「生育」：一个属就是可追溯到共同出生的一类。

normal.en: The plural is genera, and the codes require it; genuses is a sign of amateur use.
normal.cn: 复数是 genera，法规要求如此；genuses 是外行的标志。

normal.en: The binomial is genus plus species epithet, as in Panthera leo.
normal.cn: 双名法是属名加种加词，如 Panthera leo。

normal.en: A family is named after its type genus, which anchors the name.
normal.cn: 科以模式属命名，模式属因此成为名称的锚。

normal.en: Generic drifted from 'of a genus' to 'common to a class' to 'unbranded'.
normal.cn: generic 从「属的」漂移到「整类共有的」，再漂移到「无品牌的」。

abstract.en: Picture a street name that covers many houses, each with its own number.
abstract.cn: 想象一个街名覆盖许多房子，每座房子有自己的门牌号。

abstract.en: Picture a family name shared by cousins who would not recognize each other.
abstract.cn: 想象一个姓氏被彼此不认识的表亲共用。

abstract.en: Picture a box marked 'kind of kinds', holding smaller boxes also marked that way.
abstract.cn: 想象一个写着「类之类」的盒子，里面装着同样标注的小盒子。

examples.en: The genus was split when molecular data showed two unrelated lineages.
examples.cn: 当分子数据显出两条无关谱系时，这个属被拆分了。

examples.en: After the first mention, the genus name is abbreviated to one letter.
examples.cn: 首次提及之后，属名缩写为一个字母。

examples.en: In the old logic, genus and species were relations, not organisms.
examples.cn: 在旧逻辑中，属与种是关系，而不是生物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「gen 生 + us 我们」——同一个根生出来的一群 → genus 属

root: 拉丁 genus, generis「出生、族类、种类」，与 gignere「生育」相关；复数为 genera。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of genus move from the rank itself to its place in a binomial, its logical past, its everyday breadth, its Latin plural, the type genus, the monotypic case and finally the drift visible in generic.
sensesIntro.cn: genus 的八个义项从阶元本身出发，依次是双名法中的位置、逻辑学的前身、日常的宽度、拉丁复数、模式属、单型属，最后是 generic 中可见的语义漂移。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a named box of kinds, sitting inside a larger box and holding smaller ones.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只装着各种「类」的命名盒子，它本身在更大的盒子里，又装着更小的盒子。

branches.en: THE RANK AND ITS ADDRESS: the genus is both a level and the street half of a binomial.
branches.cn: 阶元与地址：属既是一个层级，也是双名法地址中的街道部分。

branches.en: LOGIC AND EVERYDAY USE: containment and 'a kind of' keep the pre-biological meaning alive.
branches.cn: 逻辑与日常：包含关系与「一类」使生物学之前的意义继续存活。

branches.en: THE FORM: the Latin plural genera is obligatory in technical prose.
branches.cn: 形式：技术文献中必须使用拉丁复数 genera。

branches.en: ANCHOR AND EDGE CASE: the type genus fixes a family name, and a monotypic genus adds no information.
branches.cn: 锚点与边界情形：模式属固定科名，单型属则不增加信息。

branches.en: THE DERIVED DRIFT: generic moved from 'of a genus' to 'shared by a class' to 'unbranded'.
branches.cn: 派生漂移：generic 从「属的」变为「整类共有的」，再变为「无品牌的」。

intro.en: Genus is one Latin noun with a double life: a word for birth and lineage, and a word for a kind that contains kinds.
intro.cn: genus 是一个有双重生命的拉丁名词：既指出生与血统，也指容纳更小种类的种类。

latinIntro.en: Latin genus gives genus, genera, generic, generate, generation, genius and genital; gignere is the verb behind them all.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 genus 给出 genus、genera、generic、generate、generation、genius、genital；gignere 是它们背后的动词。

items.example: Genus is both a lineage word and a category word.
items.exampleCN: genus 既是血统词，也是类别词。

items.example: The verb supplies the sense of common birth.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「共同出生」的意思。

items.example: Three genera share the family.
items.exampleCN: 三个属共享这个科。

items.meaning: of a genus; common to a class
items.example: The generic name appears on the label.
items.exampleCN: 标签上写着属名。

items.example: The same root produced generate and generation.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根产生 generate 与 generation。

items.example: Genius is a cousin, not a synonym of genus.
items.exampleCN: genius 是远亲，而非 genus 的同义词。

items.example: Gens names a human lineage, not a taxonomic rank.
items.exampleCN: gens 指人的血统群体，而非分类阶元。

items.example: Greek genesis is a cousin through the same ancient root.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语 genesis 经同一古老词根成为远亲。

definition_zh: 刺激；刺激物；激励因素：引起反应或推动行动的外在作用，也指实验或生理学中呈现的刺激信号
definition_en: an external event or agent that arouses a response or drives action, especially a signal presented in an experiment
core_image: 一根细尖的刺棒轻碰牲畜后腿，动物向前迈步；刺棒本身停在原处，动作由被碰的一方发出
scene: 细尖的刺棒轻碰牲畜后腿，动物立刻向前迈了一步，刺棒却始终停在原处。 In the experiment, a brief light flash served as the stimulus that started every trial.
sceneCN: 这里指引起反应的外在作用（第 1 个义项：刺激的一般定义）；句意为实验中一次短暂闪光充当启动每一轮的刺激。

pos.zh: 刺激；刺激物（可数，复数 stimuli）
激励因素；促进因素（抽象用法）

derivatives.zh: stimulus + -ate（动词化）→ 施加刺激，使产生反应
stimulate + -ion（动作或结果）→ 刺激作用或其过程
stimulate + -ive（具有……性质的）→ 具有刺激作用的
stimulare + -ant（施动者）→ 使人兴奋的物质，语义偏移为「兴奋剂」
stimulate + -or（施动者或装置）→ 发出刺激的人或装置

senses.title: An external event that arouses a response
senses.definition: an event, object or change in the environment that produces a response in a person, animal or system
senses.definitionCN: 在人、动物或系统中引起反应的事件、对象或环境变化
senses.example: A loud noise is a stimulus that makes the heart rate rise.
senses.exampleCN: 巨响是一种使心率上升的刺激。
senses.why: Latin stimulus was the goad that made an animal move, so the core is 'something that starts motion in another'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 stimulus 是驱赶牲畜前进的刺棒，核心义是「使另一方动起来的东西」。

senses.title: A concrete stimulus object
senses.definition: a particular thing presented to the senses, such as a light, a sound or a touch
senses.definitionCN: 呈现给感官的某一具体之物，如光、声或触碰
senses.example: The red square was the stimulus; the button press was the response.
senses.exampleCN: 红色方块是刺激物，按键是反应。
senses.why: the abstract event and the physical thing are the same role seen twice, so the noun covers both.
senses.whyCN: 抽象事件与物理对象是同一角色的两种看法，因此名词兼指两者。

senses.title: A signal in an experiment
senses.definition: a controlled cue presented on a schedule so that responses can be timed and counted
senses.definitionCN: 按程序呈现的受控提示，使反应能被计时与计数
senses.example: Each trial began with a visual stimulus held for half a second.
senses.exampleCN: 每一轮都以一个持续半秒的视觉刺激开始。
senses.why: a laboratory needs the goad to be exactly repeatable, so stimulus became the word for the timed cue.
senses.whyCN: 实验室需要刺棒能精确重复，于是 stimulus 成了计时提示的词。

senses.title: Sensory input
senses.definition: light, sound, smell, taste or touch that reaches a sense organ and can be detected
senses.definitionCN: 到达感觉器官并可被察觉的光、声、气味、味道或触感
senses.example: The retina needs a minimum level of light stimulus to register anything.
senses.exampleCN: 视网膜需要最低限度的光刺激才能记录任何东西。
senses.why: physiology narrowed the word to whatever the senses can take in, whether or not a person notices.
senses.whyCN: 生理学把这个词收窄到感官能接收的东西，无论人是否注意到。

senses.title: Electrical stimulation of nerves
senses.definition: a controlled electrical pulse applied to a nerve or muscle to evoke a response
senses.definitionCN: 施加于神经或肌肉以引发反应的受控电脉冲
senses.example: A brief electrical stimulus made the frog's leg twitch.
senses.exampleCN: 一次短暂的电刺激使蛙腿抽动。
senses.why: electricity let experimenters apply the goad directly to tissue, and the word followed the method.
senses.whyCN: 电让实验者能把刺棒直接加在组织上，词也跟着方法走。

senses.title: A policy or economic incentive
senses.titleCN: 政策或经济上的刺激措施
senses.definition: a measure such as spending or a tax cut intended to make an economy or market act
senses.definitionCN: 支出或减税等旨在使经济或市场行动起来的手段
senses.example: The government offered a stimulus to small builders.
senses.exampleCN: 政府向小型建筑商提供了刺激措施。
senses.why: the image of prodding an animal transfers easily to prodding an economy into motion.
senses.whyCN: 驱赶动物的形象很容易转移到驱赶经济使其动起来。

senses.title: A spur to action or thought
senses.titleCN: 促使人行动或思考的因素
senses.definition: something that incites a person or group to act, create or think further
senses.definitionCN: 促使个人或群体行动、创造或进一步思考的东西
senses.example: The exhibition was the stimulus for a decade of new work.
senses.exampleCN: 这场展览成了此后十年新创作的刺激。
senses.why: the figurative Latin sense 'that which incites' survived alongside the physical one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语中「激起者」的比喻义与物理义一同存活下来。

senses.title: An environmental trigger in biology
senses.titleCN: 生物学中的环境触发因素
senses.definition: a change such as temperature, light or food that triggers a behavioural or physiological response
senses.definitionCN: 温度、光照或食物等触发行为或生理反应的变化
senses.example: Shortening days are the stimulus for the birds' migration.
senses.exampleCN: 白昼变短是鸟类迁徙的触发因素。
senses.why: ecology adopted the word because an organism's action always begins with something outside it.
senses.whyCN: 生态学采用这个词，因为生物的行动总由外部某物开始。

senses.title: A provocation to reflection
senses.definition: a question, image or event that sets off thought without requiring a physical reaction
senses.definitionCN: 引发思考、但不要求身体反应的问题、图像或事件
senses.example: The teacher used one odd photograph as a stimulus for discussion.
senses.exampleCN: 老师用一张古怪的照片作为讨论的刺激。
senses.why: when the response is mental rather than muscular, the same word still names what set it going.
senses.whyCN: 当反应是心理的而非肌肉的，同一个词仍指那个让它启动的东西。

intro.en: Stimulus is a Latin noun that English borrowed whole. Its first image is a pointed stick used to prod animals, and the figurative sense of 'incitement' came with it. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: stimulus 是英语整体借入的拉丁名词。它最初的形象是驱赶牲畜的尖头棒，「激励、激起」的比喻义也随之而来。年代为约数。

items.en: Stimulus meant 'a goad, a prick, a spur', the pointed stick that made a draft animal move forward. The word named the tool, not the animal's reaction.
items.cn: stimulus 意为「刺棒、尖刺、马刺」，即使役畜前进的尖头棒。这个词命名工具，而非动物的反应。

items.en: The verb stimulare meant 'to goad, prick, urge on', and its participle could describe a person driven to act.
items.cn: 动词 stimulare 意为「驱赶、刺、催促」，其分词可以描述被驱动而行动的人。

items.en: Latin prose already used stimulus for 'that which incites or provokes', so the mental sense is not a modern invention.
items.cn: 拉丁散文已用 stimulus 指「激起或挑动之物」，因此心理层面的意思并非近代发明。

items.en: English took stimulus in the seventeenth century, first in learned prose about bodies, spirits and whatever sets them in motion.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪借入 stimulus，最初用于论身体、精气以及使之运动的因素的学术散文。

items.en: In the nineteenth century physiology and psychology made stimulus a technical term for input that evokes a response, and the plural stimuli was kept as a Latin plural.
items.cn: 19 世纪生理学与心理学把 stimulus 变成指「引起反应的输入」的术语，复数 stimuli 则保留拉丁复数形式。

items.en: Reconstructed form (deeper root): the connection of the Latin noun to an Indo-European root for 'to prick, goad' is a hypothesis, and every form proposed for that root is a reconstruction; the noun itself and its verb stimulare are documented in Latin.
items.cn: 重构形式（更深词根）：把这个拉丁名词与印欧语「刺、扎」词根相连只是假说，为该词根提出的形式全是重构；这个名词本身及其动词 stimulare 在拉丁语中有书证。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same stem that are often confused; group two holds words that also push someone to act but come from different roots.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干、常被混淆的形式；第二组是同样促使人行动、但词根不同的词。

entries.definition: A drug or drink that raises activity in the body; it is a substance taken, while a stimulus is an event presented.
entries.definitionCN: 提高身体活动的药物或饮料，是被摄入的物质；stimulus 是被呈现的事件。

entries.definition: The action of applying a stimulus; the noun names the cause, the verb names the causing.
entries.definitionCN: 施加刺激的动作；名词指原因，动词指施加。

entries.definition: The Latin plural of stimulus; using it for a single event is a common error.
entries.definitionCN: stimulus 的拉丁复数；用它指单一事件是常见错误。

entries.definition: A signal that tells someone when or what to do; it is usually intentional, while a stimulus may be merely present.
entries.definitionCN: 告诉人何时或做什么的信号，通常是有意发出的；stimulus 可以只是存在着。

entries.definition: Something offered to make people want to act, usually a reward; it works through desire, not through direct evocation.
entries.definitionCN: 为让人愿意行动而提供的东西，通常是奖励；它通过欲望起作用，而非直接引发反应。

entries.definition: The immediate cause that sets off an already prepared response, as a trigger releases a spring.
entries.definitionCN: 引发已准备好之反应的直接原因，如扳机松开弹簧。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real scientific collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实科学搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Picture the goad before the animal moves: the word names the prod, not the step.
normal.cn: 先想象牲畜移动之前的刺棒：这个词命名的是那一下刺，而不是那一步。

normal.en: The family runs stimulate, stimulation, stimulative, stimulant, stimulator.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 stimulate、stimulation、stimulative、stimulant、stimulator。

normal.en: Fixed pairs mark the science: stimulus and response, sensory stimulus, present a stimulus.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出科学用法：刺激与反应、感官刺激、呈现刺激。

normal.en: The plural is Latin: one stimulus, two stimuli, with the -us changing to -i.
normal.cn: 复数是拉丁式：一个 stimulus，两个 stimuli，-us 变为 -i。

normal.en: The policy phrase economic stimulus keeps the old image of prodding something into motion.
normal.cn: 政策短语 economic stimulus 保留了「把某物戳动起来」的旧形象。

abstract.en: Picture a finger tapping a sleeping animal and stepping back.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指轻点睡着的动物，然后退开。

abstract.en: Picture a switch on the outside of a machine, never inside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个装在机器外部的开关，从不在内部。

abstract.en: Picture a spark that lights a fuse and then disappears.
abstract.cn: 想象一点火星点燃引线，随后自己消失。

examples.en: The same stimulus produced different responses in different subjects.
examples.cn: 同一个刺激在不同受试者身上产生了不同反应。

examples.en: Without a stimulus, the reflex cannot be observed at all.
examples.cn: 没有刺激，反射根本无法被观察到。

examples.en: Economists argued about how large the stimulus should be.
examples.cn: 经济学家争论刺激措施应该多大。

dict_mnemonic.text: stimulus 原指驱赶牲畜的尖刺棒；记「刺棒不动，被刺的一方动」。

root: 拉丁 stimulus「刺棒、尖刺、马刺」，动词 stimulare「驱赶、刺、催促」；更早来源不确定，与印欧语「刺、扎」词根的联系仅为假说，所拟形式属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one goad: it is a physical prod, then a presented object, a timed cue, a sensory input, an electric pulse, a policy measure, a spur to thought, an environmental trigger and a provocation to reflection.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿着同一根刺棒展开：它是物理的刺、被呈现的物件、计时提示、感官输入、电脉冲、政策手段、思考的推动、环境触发因素，最后是引发反思的契机。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pointed stick touching an animal's flank; the stick stays still, the step belongs to the animal.
core.cn: 核心意象：尖头棒碰到牲畜肋侧；棒子不动，迈出的那一步属于牲畜。

branches.en: THE CAUSE: one event outside the organism sets a response going.
branches.cn: 原因：有机体之外的某一事件使反应启动。

branches.en: THE OBJECT AND THE CUE: the same role can be a physical thing or a timed signal in a trial.
branches.cn: 物件与提示：同一角色可以是一个实物，也可以是实验中计时的信号。

branches.en: TWO ENERGIES: light reaching an eye and current reaching a nerve are both input.
branches.cn: 两种能量：到达眼睛的光与到达神经的电流都是输入。

branches.en: THE ECONOMY AND THE MIND: a budget measure and a striking image both prod something into motion.
branches.cn: 经济与心智：一项预算措施与一个醒目的图像，都在把某物戳动起来。

branches.en: NATURE AND REFLECTION: a change of season triggers migration, and a question triggers thought.
branches.cn: 自然与反思：季节变化触发迁徙，一个问题触发思考。

intro.en: Stimulus is a Latin noun with a small but productive English family, all built on the same stem with verb, noun and adjective suffixes.
intro.cn: stimulus 是一个拉丁名词，带有一个小而多产的英语词族，全部由同一词干加动词、名词与形容词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin stimulus and stimulare supply the stem; the suffix -atio later gives stimulation, and -ant gives stimulant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 stimulus 与 stimulare 提供词干；后缀 -atio 后来给出 stimulation，-ant 给出 stimulant。

items.example: The noun named the tool before it named the reaction.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词先命名工具，后命名反应。

items.example: The verb turns the stick into an action.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把棒子变成动作。

items.example: The action noun supplies the English -tion form.
items.exampleCN: 这个动作名词提供英语的 -tion 形式。

items.example: The verb is the everyday member of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是词族中最日常的一员。

items.meaning: the act or result of stimulating
items.example: The noun is common in physiology and electronics.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词常见于生理学与电子学。

items.example: The adjective often describes policy.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词常描述政策。

items.example: The noun narrowed to drugs and drinks.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词收窄到药物与饮料。

items.meaning: one or a device that stimulates
items.example: The device sense is common in medicine.
items.exampleCN: 装置义在医学中常见。

items.example: The Latin plural survives in scientific English.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁复数在科学英语中留存。

definition_zh: 杏仁；扁桃仁；扁桃树；杏仁色（浅褐米色）
definition_en: the edible seed of the almond tree, oval and pointed at both ends, eaten as a nut or ground into flour; also a pale warm brown colour
core_image: 一颗藏在硬壳里、两头尖尖的浅褐色种子
scene: 她把坚果磨成粉，做成了圣诞蛋糕。 Almond flour gives the cake its dense texture.
sceneCN: 这里 almond 是「杏仁」（第 1 个义项：扁桃树的种子，常作坚果食用）；句意为杏仁粉让蛋糕质地紧实。核心画面是一颗藏在硬壳里、两头尖尖的浅褐色种子。

pos.zh: 杏仁；扁桃；杏仁色

derivatives.zh: 加 -ine 构成，义为「以杏仁烹制的」
同希腊词根，义为「杏仁状体；大脑杏仁核」
加 -in 构成，义为「杏仁苷」

senses.title: The nut of the almond tree
senses.definition: the edible seed of the almond tree, oval and pointed at both ends, eaten as a nut or ground into flour
senses.definitionCN: 扁桃树的可食种子，椭圆形、两端尖，作坚果食用或磨成粉
senses.example: She scattered toasted almonds over the salad.
senses.exampleCN: 她把烤过的杏仁撒在沙拉上。
senses.why: The word came from Greek amygdale, almond, through Latin and French, and the l was reinserted by scholars who knew the Latin spelling.
senses.whyCN: 该词来自希腊语 amygdale「杏仁」，经拉丁语与法语传入，其中的 l 是懂拉丁拼写的学者重新加回去的。

senses.title: A pale warm brown colour
senses.definition: a pale, slightly warm brown colour like the skin of the nut, used in design and cosmetics
senses.definitionCN: 像杏仁外皮那样浅而略暖的褐色，用于设计与化妆品
senses.example: The walls were painted a soft almond.
senses.exampleCN: 墙面漆成了柔和的杏仁色。
senses.why: Here the nut lends its skin colour to the word, the same transfer that gives us chocolate, olive and salmon.
senses.whyCN: 这里坚果把它外皮的颜色借给了这个词，与 chocolate、olive、salmon 的转移方式相同。

intro.en: Almond travelled from Greek amygdale through Latin amygdala and Old French almande; the l in the modern spelling is a scholarly restoration.
intro.cn: almond 从希腊语 amygdale 经拉丁语 amygdala 与古法语 almande 一路走来；现代拼写中的 l 是学者恢复的。

items.en: Greek amygdale meant almond, and it also named anything shaped like one, including a part of the brain.
items.cn: 希腊语 amygdale 意为杏仁，也指任何杏仁形状的东西，包括大脑的一个部分。

items.en: Latin amygdala kept both the nut and the shape sense, and gave English the anatomical term amygdala.
items.cn: 拉丁语 amygdala 保留坚果与形状两义，并为英语提供解剖学术语 amygdala。

items.en: Old French almande lost the g and the y, and the word entered Middle English as almande or almaunde.
items.cn: 古法语 almande 丢掉了 g 与 y，该词以 almande 或 almaunde 的形式进入中古英语。

items.en: Scribes who knew Latin put the l back, and by the fifteenth century almond was the usual spelling.
items.cn: 懂拉丁语的书吏把 l 加了回去，到十五世纪 almond 成为常见拼写。

items.en: Modern almond names the nut, the tree, its milk and flour, and a pale brown colour used in design.
items.cn: 现代 almond 指坚果、树、它的奶与粉，以及设计中用到的一种浅褐色。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps words of similar shape; the near-meaning group lists other nuts and a neighbouring colour.
note.cn: 形近组保留形状相近的词；近义组列出其他坚果与相邻的颜色。

entries.definition: Money given to the poor.

entries.definition: To change something for the better.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物改得更好。

entries.definition: Cooked or garnished with almonds.
entries.definitionCN: 用杏仁烹制或点缀的。

entries.definition: A wrinkled nut in a hard round shell.
entries.definitionCN: 硬圆壳里带皱纹的坚果。

entries.definition: A small round brown nut.
entries.definitionCN: 小而圆的褐色坚果。

entries.definition: A kidney-shaped nut.
entries.definitionCN: 肾形的坚果。

entries.definition: A pale sandy brown colour.

normalIntro.en: Almond comes from Greek amygdale, and the brain amygdala is named after the same nut shape.
normalIntro.cn: almond 来自希腊语 amygdale，大脑的 amygdala（杏仁核）正是按同一种坚果形状命名的。

normal.en: Almond and amygdala share one Greek root, so the brain region is literally almond-shaped.
normal.cn: almond 与 amygdala 共享一个希腊词根，所以那个脑区字面就是「杏仁形的」。

normal.en: The l is written but not pronounced: say AH-mund, not AL-mond.
normal.cn: l 写出来但不发音：读作 AH-mund，不是 AL-mond。

normal.en: Almond flour is ground nuts; almond milk is soaked and blended nuts.
normal.cn: almond flour 是磨碎的坚果，almond milk 是浸泡后打碎的坚果。

normal.en: It is countable as a nut, so say six almonds, but uncountable as a colour.
normal.cn: 指坚果时可数，所以说 six almonds；指颜色时不可数。

normal.en: Botanically the almond is a seed, not a true nut, but the kitchen calls it a nut.
normal.cn: 植物学上杏仁是种子，不是真正的坚果，但厨房里叫它坚果。

abstract.en: Picture a pointed brown seed inside a woody shell.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗两头尖的褐色种子藏在木质硬壳里。

abstract.en: Imagine an orchard of small trees with pale pink blossom.
abstract.cn: 想象一片小树林，开着淡粉色的花。

abstract.en: Think of a colour card the shade of the nut skin.
abstract.cn: 想象一张色卡，正是坚果外皮的那个色度。

examples.en: The recipe calls for ground almonds and no wheat flour.
examples.cn: 这个配方要用杏仁粉，不用小麦面粉。

examples.en: Almond trees blossom early in the valley.
examples.cn: 山谷里的扁桃树开花很早。

examples.en: She chose almond for the bedroom walls.
examples.cn: 她为卧室墙面选了杏仁色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿蒙德」——阿（al）蒙（mon）德（d）：硬壳里蒙着一颗尖头种子，就是杏仁。

root: 希腊语 amygdale「杏仁」经拉丁语 amygdala 与古法语 almande 进入中古英语，懂拉丁语的书吏把 l 加回拼写，形成 almond；同一词根还产生解剖学词 amygdala「杏仁核」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses come from one seed: the first names the nut you eat, and the second borrows the pale brown of its skin as a colour name.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都来自同一颗种子：第一个指你吃的坚果，第二个借它外皮的浅褐色作为颜色名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pointed brown seed in a hard shell
core.cn: 核心意象：硬壳里一颗两头尖的褐色种子

branches.en: A handful of toasted nuts.
branches.cn: 一把烤过的坚果。

branches.en: Flour ground from blanched kernels.
branches.cn: 用去皮仁磨成的粉。

branches.en: A pale warm wall colour.
branches.cn: 浅而暖的墙面色。

branches.en: A lipstick shade named after the skin.
branches.cn: 以外皮命名的唇膏色号。

branches.en: Both start from the same seed.
branches.cn: 两者都从同一颗种子出发。

intro.en: Almond has no productive English affixes, but its Greek root amygdal- still builds scientific words, and -ine forms the cooking adjective.
intro.cn: almond 没有能产的英语词缀，但它的希腊词根 amygdal- 仍在造科学词，-ine 则构成烹饪形容词。

latinIntro.en: Greek amygdale passed into Latin amygdala and then into Old French almande, where the g and y were lost.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 amygdale 进入拉丁语成为 amygdala，再进入古法语成为 almande，途中丢掉了 g 与 y。
