definition_zh: 扩大的；膨胀的；展开的；扩展的
definition_en: growing larger in size, scope or number, or opening out from a folded or compressed state
core_image: 一只气球被不断吹大，表面的墨点彼此越离越远
scene: 吹气口接着气泵，橡胶表面上的墨点随着体积增大而彼此远离。 The expanding balloon pushed its painted dots farther apart.
sceneCN: 这里指「体积不断变大的」（第 1 个义项：物体受内压或加热而向外胀大）；句意为膨胀的气球把画上的墨点推得越来越远。图中可辨识物件：气球、气泵、墨点、细绳。

pos.zh: 扩大中的；膨胀的；展开的
expand 的现在分词（正在扩大）

senses.title: Growing larger in volume
senses.definition: becoming larger in volume, as a gas, a balloon or heated metal
senses.definitionCN: 体积变大，如气体、气球或受热的金属
senses.example: The expanding balloon pushed its painted dots farther apart.
senses.exampleCN: 膨胀的气球把画上的墨点推得越来越远。
senses.why: expanding is the present participle of expand, so it names an ongoing increase rather than a finished state.
senses.whyCN: expanding 是 expand 的现在分词，因此指正在进行的增大，而非已完成的状态。

senses.title: Extending in scope
senses.definition: growing to cover more activities, customers or territory
senses.definitionCN: 扩展到覆盖更多业务、客户或地域
senses.example: The expanding company opened three new offices.
senses.exampleCN: 这家扩张中的公司新开了三处办公室。
senses.why: the physical sense of spreading outward was applied to organisations and their reach.
senses.whyCN: 向外铺展的物理义被用于组织及其覆盖面。

senses.title: Opening something folded
senses.definition: unfolding or spreading out something that was compressed
senses.definitionCN: 把被压缩或折叠的东西摊开
senses.example: The expanding map covered the whole table.
senses.exampleCN: 展开的地图铺满了整张桌子。
senses.why: the Latin root pandere meant 'to spread', and English kept that literal gesture.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 pandere 意为「铺开」，英语保留了这一具体动作。

senses.title: Developing an account in detail
senses.definition: developing a statement, story or argument at greater length
senses.definitionCN: 把陈述、故事或论证写得更长更细
senses.example: Her expanding notes turned into a full chapter.
senses.exampleCN: 她不断展开的笔记变成了一整章。
senses.why: writing that grows longer is pictured as a surface being spread out.
senses.whyCN: 越写越长的文字，被想象成一张被铺开的平面。

senses.title: The universe expanding
senses.definition: the increase of space itself, carrying galaxies apart
senses.definitionCN: 空间本身的增长，使星系彼此远离
senses.example: The expanding universe carries distant galaxies away from one another.
senses.exampleCN: 膨胀的宇宙使遥远星系彼此远离。
senses.why: cosmology reused the everyday verb for space itself, not for matter moving into empty room.
senses.whyCN: 宇宙学把这个日常动词用于空间本身，而不是物质在空房间里运动。

senses.title: Writing out a mathematical expression
senses.definition: rewriting an expression as a sum or product of simpler terms
senses.definitionCN: 把一个式子改写为更简单项的和或积
senses.example: The expanding series revealed a simple pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 展开后的级数显出一个简单规律。
senses.why: algebra speaks of expanding brackets because the written expression literally takes up more space.
senses.whyCN: 代数说「展开括号」，是因为写出来的式子确实占了更多空间。

senses.title: Increasing in number
senses.definition: growing in number, membership or quantity
senses.definitionCN: 数量、成员或总量增长
senses.example: The expanding list of members forced a larger hall.
senses.exampleCN: 不断增长的成员名单迫使换更大的礼堂。
senses.why: once scope widens, the count behind it rises, so the same participle covers numbers.
senses.whyCN: 范围一旦变宽，背后的数量就会上升，因此同一分词也覆盖数量。

senses.title: Spreading open
senses.definition: opening out something held closed, such as wings or a chest
senses.definitionCN: 把合拢的东西张开，如翅膀或胸膛
senses.example: The expanding wings caught the warm air.
senses.exampleCN: 张开的翅膀兜住暖空气。
senses.why: the oldest literal sense of spreading survives in the body and in machinery.
senses.whyCN: 「铺开」这一最古老的字面义，仍留在身体与机械的用法中。

intro.en: Expanding is the present participle of expand, from Latin expandere 'to spread out', built on ex- 'out' and pandere 'to spread'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: expanding 是 expand 的现在分词，来自拉丁 expandere「铺开」，由 ex-「向外」与 pandere「铺展」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pandere meant 'to spread out, open' and also supplied the base of the word for a spreading roof. Its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: pandere 意为「铺开、张开」，也是表示「展开的屋顶」一词的词基。其更深来源不确定。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus pandere produced expandere 'to spread out, unfold', used of hands, wings and written matter.
items.cn: ex-「向外」加 pandere 构成 expandere「铺开、展开」，用于手、翅膀与文字材料。

items.en: The verb entered English in the fifteenth century through French, first in the sense of spreading something out.
items.cn: 这个动词在十五世纪经法语进入英语，最初指把某物摊开。

items.en: From the seventeenth century gases and metals were said to expand when heated, fixing the volume sense.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，气体与金属受热时被说成 expand，从而固定了体积义。

items.en: Twentieth-century cosmology applied the participle to space itself, giving the expanding universe.
items.cn: 二十世纪的宇宙学把这个分词用于空间本身，形成了「膨胀的宇宙」。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the pre-Latin origin of pandere is not established, and any Indo-European root proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：pandere 在拉丁语之前的来源未得到证明，凡为其提出的印欧词根均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root forms that look alike; group two holds near-meaning growth words.
note.cn: 第一组是同根形近形式；第二组是语义相近的增长词。

entries.definition: The verb itself, naming the event; expanding names the event in progress or the thing undergoing it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词本身，指事件；expanding 指进行中的事件或正在经历它的东西。

entries.definition: The past participle, describing something that has already grown; expanding is still in motion.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词，描述已经长大的东西；expanding 仍在进行中。

entries.definition: Describing something broad or tending to expand, often a mood or a view, not an active process.
entries.definitionCN: 描述开阔或趋于扩张的事物，多指心境或视野，而非进行中的过程。

entries.definition: The act or result of expanding; the participle points to the process, the noun to the process as a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 扩张的动作或结果；分词指向过程，名词把过程当作事物。

entries.definition: Increasing in size or number by natural development; expanding stresses outward spread.
entries.definitionCN: 经自然发育而增大或增多；expanding 强调向外铺展。

entries.definition: Becoming larger because of internal pressure or fluid; it is more physical and often unwanted.
entries.definitionCN: 因内部压力或液体而变大；更偏物理，且常含不希望的意味。

entries.definition: Increasing in width; expanding can happen in any direction or in abstract scope.
entries.definitionCN: 宽度增加；expanding 可在任何方向或抽象范围发生。

entries.definition: Becoming longer under tension; it need not add material or volume.
entries.definitionCN: 在拉力下变长；不一定增加材料或体积。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的语素与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ex- 'out' plus pandere 'spread': to spread outward.
normal.cn: ex-「向外」加 pandere「铺展」：向外铺开。

normal.en: The family runs expand, expansion, expansive, expandable.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 expand、expansion、expansive、expandable。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: expanding universe, expanding market, expanding foam.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：膨胀的宇宙、扩张的市场、膨胀泡沫。

normal.en: Expanding brackets in algebra literally takes up more paper.
normal.cn: 代数里展开括号，字面上确实占了更多纸面。

normal.en: The participle is active; expanded is finished.
normal.cn: 分词形式是进行中的；expanded 是已完成的。

abstract.en: Picture a balloon whose dots drift apart as it fills.
abstract.cn: 想象气球被吹大时，表面的墨点彼此漂远。

abstract.en: Picture a map unfolded until it covers the table.
abstract.cn: 想象地图被摊开，直到铺满桌面。

abstract.en: Picture a city that keeps pushing its edge outward each year.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市每年把边缘向外推。

examples.en: The expanding universe is not expanding into anything.
examples.cn: 膨胀的宇宙并不是在向某个东西里膨胀。

examples.en: The company is expanding into three new markets.
examples.cn: 这家公司正在向三个新市场扩张。

examples.en: An expanding gas does work on the piston.
examples.cn: 膨胀的气体对活塞做功。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（向外）+ pand（铺展）+ ing（进行）」——正在向外铺开 → 扩大的、膨胀的

root: 拉丁 expandere「铺开」= ex-「向外」+ pandere「铺展」；pandere 更深来源不确定，其印欧词根一说属重构。英语 expand 经法语进入，expanding 为其现在分词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one outward movement: volume swells, scope widens, a folded thing opens, an account lengthens, space itself grows, algebra spreads, numbers rise and wings open.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一次向外运动：体积胀大、范围变宽、折叠物打开、叙述变长、空间本身增长、代数式铺开、数量上升、翅膀张开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balloon filling with air, every mark on its skin moving away from every other.
core.cn: 核心意象：气球被充气，表面每个标记都离其他标记越来越远。

branches.en: VOLUME AND SPACE: from a balloon to the universe, the same outward swell.
branches.cn: 体积与空间：从气球到宇宙，同一种向外的胀大。

branches.en: SCOPE AND COUNT: wider reach brings more members and more territory.
branches.cn: 范围与数量：覆盖更广带来更多成员与更多地域。

branches.en: UNFOLDING AND OPENING: what was closed spreads open again.
branches.cn: 摊开与张开：原本合拢的重新铺开。

branches.en: DETAIL: a text occupies more space as it develops.
branches.cn: 细节：文本随展开而占据更多空间。

branches.en: ALGEBRA: symbols take up more paper when brackets are expanded.
branches.cn: 代数：展开括号后，符号占更多纸面。

intro.en: Expanding is built from the Latin verb expandere, whose prefix and root both recur in English.
intro.cn: expanding 来自拉丁动词 expandere，其前缀与词根都在英语中复现。

latinIntro.en: Ex- 'out' plus pandere 'to spread' gives expandere; the same pandere underlies expanse and the older sense of a spread roof.
latinIntro.cn: ex-「向外」加 pandere「铺展」构成 expandere；同一 pandere 还构成 expanse，以及「展开的屋顶」这一较旧义。

items.example: The prefix turns spreading into spreading outward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「铺」变成「向外铺」。

items.example: Pandere is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: pandere 是整个词族的词根。

items.example: Metals expand when heated.
items.exampleCN: 金属受热会膨胀。

items.example: The expanding gas did work.
items.exampleCN: 膨胀的气体做了功。

items.meaning: the act or result of expanding
items.example: The expansion of the market was rapid.
items.exampleCN: 市场的扩张很迅速。

items.example: The view was expansive.
items.exampleCN: 视野很开阔。

items.example: The drive is expandable.
items.exampleCN: 这个硬盘可扩展。

items.example: A flat expanse of salt lay ahead.
items.exampleCN: 前方是一片平坦的盐滩。

items.example: The gas is expansible under heat.
items.exampleCN: 这种气体受热可膨胀。

definition_zh: 年表；年代学；时间顺序；大事记
definition_en: the study of dates and time order, or an ordered list of events arranged by when they happened
core_image: 一串日期标签钉在一条长线上，最早的在左端，最近的在右端
scene: 侦探在白板上画出一条横线，把案发、报警、到场、离开的时刻依次写上去。 The detective draws a line on the board and writes the times of the crime, the call, the arrival and the departure: that line is the chronology of the case.
sceneCN: 这里指第 1 个义项。这里 chronology 是「时间线、事件年表」（第 1、7 个义项：有序事件清单与案件时间线）；句意：侦探把案发、报警、到场、离开的时刻依次写在一条横线上，这条线就是案件的时间线。图中可辨识物件：白板、横线、时间标签、马克笔。

pos.zh: 年表；年代学；时间顺序

forms.label: 复数（指多份年表或多种年代体系）

derivatives.zh: 按时间顺序的；年代学的

senses.title: An ordered list of events
senses.titleCN: 按顺序排列的事件清单
senses.definition: a list that sets events out in the order in which they occurred
senses.definitionCN: 按事件发生的先后顺序列出事件的清单
senses.example: The report opens with a chronology of the negotiations.
senses.exampleCN: 报告开头是一份谈判事件的时间表。
senses.why: This is the most concrete sense: a list you could print. The noun names the product, not the method behind it.
senses.whyCN: 这是最具体的义项：一份可以打印出来的清单。这个名词命名的是产物，而不是背后的方法。

senses.title: The discipline of dating
senses.definition: the scholarly study of dates and how they are established
senses.definitionCN: 对日期以及日期如何被确定的学术研究
senses.example: He teaches chronology at the institute of history.
senses.exampleCN: 他在历史研究所教授年代学。
senses.why: The -logy in the word promises a field, not a list. This sense treats chronology as a method with rules for testing dates.
senses.whyCN: 词中的 -logy 许诺的是一个领域，而不是一份清单。这一义把 chronology 当作一门有检验日期规则的方法。

senses.title: The order itself
senses.definition: the actual temporal relation between events, independent of any list
senses.definitionCN: 事件之间真实的时间关系，不依赖任何清单
senses.example: The chronology of the two outbreaks is still unclear.
senses.exampleCN: 两次爆发的先后仍不清楚。
senses.why: Here the word means the relation in the world, not a record of it. Disputes over chronology are disputes about what really came first.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词指世界中的关系，而不是对它的记录。关于年代顺序的争论，就是关于究竟什么先发生的争论。

senses.title: A historical account ordered by time
senses.titleCN: 按时间编排的历史记述
senses.definition: a historical narrative or table that proceeds year by year
senses.definitionCN: 逐年推进的历史叙述或表格
senses.example: Medieval chronicles often mix chronology with legend.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪编年史常把年代记述与传说混在一起。
senses.why: Older history was written as chronology: one year after another, with little analysis. The word still carries that plain, cumulative style.
senses.whyCN: 较早的历史写作就是年表式的：一年接一年，分析很少。这个词至今带着那种朴素、累积的文体。

senses.title: Geological chronology
senses.definition: the ordering of earth history, by rock layers or by radiometric dating
senses.definitionCN: 通过岩层或放射性测年排列地球历史
senses.example: Geological chronology places the extinction at the end of the Cretaceous.
senses.exampleCN: 地质年代学把那场灭绝定位在白垩纪末。
senses.why: Earth history has no written dates, so chronology had to be rebuilt from layers and isotopes. The word moves from texts to stones.
senses.whyCN: 地球历史没有写下的日期，年代顺序必须从岩层与同位素重建。这个词从文本移到了石头。

senses.title: A biography's timeline
senses.definition: a dated outline of a person's life and main works
senses.definitionCN: 一个人生平与主要作品的带日期纲要
senses.example: The biography ends with a chronology of the poet's life.
senses.exampleCN: 传记末尾附有诗人一生的年谱。
senses.why: A single life is small enough to be put on one line. Publishers use chronology as an appendix, because readers want dates without narrative.
senses.whyCN: 一个人的一生小到可以放在一条线上。出版社把年谱作为附录，因为读者想要日期，而不想要叙述。

senses.title: A case or investigation timeline
senses.definition: the reconstructed sequence of events in an investigation or dispute
senses.definitionCN: 在调查或争议中被重建的事件顺序
senses.example: Police built a minute-by-minute chronology of the night.
senses.exampleCN: 警方建立了那一夜逐分钟的时间线。
senses.why: In legal and investigative settings chronology is a tool of proof. Gaps in the line become the questions that have to be answered.
senses.whyCN: 在法律与调查场景中，年表是证明的工具。线上的空白就成了必须回答的问题。

senses.title: Narrative order
senses.definition: the order in which a story presents events, which may differ from their actual order
senses.definitionCN: 故事呈现事件的顺序，它可以与实际发生的顺序不同
senses.example: The novel's chronology is broken by long flashbacks.
senses.exampleCN: 这部长篇的时间顺序被长段倒叙打断。
senses.why: Literary criticism uses chronology for the story's own clock. The word can therefore describe a deliberate distortion of time, not only a faithful record.
senses.whyCN: 文学批评用 chronology 指故事自身的时钟。因此这个词也能描述对时间的有意扭曲，而不只是忠实记录。

senses.title: Cosmic or evolutionary chronology
senses.definition: the very long sequence of natural history, from the universe's origin to the present
senses.definitionCN: 从宇宙起源至今的极长的自然史序列
senses.example: Cosmic chronology compresses thirteen billion years into one chart.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙年表把一百三十亿年压缩进一张图表。
senses.why: The word scales up without changing shape. Whether the units are minutes or millions of years, chronology still means one line with events placed on it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以无限放大而不变形。无论单位是分钟还是百万年，chronology 仍指一条线以及线上的事件。

intro.en: Chronology was coined in Renaissance Latin from Greek parts: khronos, 'time', and -logia, 'account, study'. It is not an ancient Greek word. English took it from French in the 16th century, and only later derived the adjective chronological from it. The noun therefore came first, and it named both a science and the tables that science produced.
intro.cn: chronology 是文艺复兴拉丁语用希腊成分造的：khronos“时间”与 -logia“记述、学问”。它不是古希腊语词。英语在 16 世纪从法语接过来，之后才由它派生出形容词 chronological。所以名词先出现，并且同时命名一门学问和这门学问产出的表格。

items.en: Khronos meant 'time' as duration or period. Its own etymology is uncertain; suggested links with roots meaning 'cut' are not accepted as proven.
items.cn: khronos 指作为时长或时期的时间。它自身的词源不确定；与“切割”类词根的关联只是提议，并未被证明。

items.en: From logos, 'word, account, reason', -logia named a branch of study. It promised a reasoned body of knowledge rather than a mere list.
items.cn: 来自 logos“言词、记述、理据”，-logia 命名一门研究分支。它许诺的是有理由的知识体系，而不只是一份清单。

items.en: The compound was assembled by late 16th-century scholars, and it is associated with the period's work on correcting historical dates. It was a technical coinage, not an inherited word.
items.cn: 这个复合词由 16 世纪晚期学者组装而成，与该时代校正历史日期的工作相关。它是技术造词，不是继承来的词。

items.en: French adopted the Latin form as chronologie. English borrowed it in the 16th century. The early English word covered both the science and the tabulated result.
items.cn: 法语把拉丁形式接为 chronologie。英语在 16 世纪借入。早期英语中，这个词同时涵盖学问与制表结果。

items.en: The two branches separated: chronology as a discipline with rules, and chronology as an appendix of dates in a book. Historians and geologists pushed the second branch into new material.
items.cn: 两个分支分开：作为有规则之学问的 chronology，以及作为书中日期附录的 chronology。历史学家与地质学家把后一支推进到新材料上。

items.en: Modern use adds geological, cosmic and investigative chronologies, and the plural chronologies for rival dating systems. The word still names both a line of events and the study of how that line is drawn.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了地质、宇宙与调查年表，以及指相互竞争的断代体系的复数 chronologies。这个词仍同时命名一条事件线，以及研究这条线如何被画出的学问。

note.en: The first group separates chronology from two derived relatives and one look-alike word from the same root. The second group compares other ways of recording ordered time.
note.cn: 第一组把 chronology 与两个派生亲属及一个同根形近词分开。第二组比较记录有序时间的其它方式。

entries.definition: arranged in time order. The adjective describes the arrangement; chronology names it.
entries.definitionCN: 按时间顺序排列的。形容词描述排列；chronology 命名排列。

entries.definition: a person who studies or establishes dates. The -ist marks the practitioner.
entries.definitionCN: 研究或确定日期的人。后缀 -ist 标示从业者。

entries.definition: a written record of events year by year. It comes from the same Greek root but is a different formation and usually names a text.
entries.definitionCN: 逐年记录事件的文字。它同出希腊词根，但构词不同，通常指一部文本。

entries.definition: a graphical line showing when events happened. It is the everyday word for what chronology often means in practice.
entries.definitionCN: 显示事件发生时间的图形线。它是 chronology 在实际使用中常指之物的日常说法。

entries.definition: a narrative record arranged year by year. A chronicle is a document; a chronology can be a bare list or a science.
entries.definitionCN: 逐年编排的叙述记录。chronicle 是一份文献；chronology 可以是纯清单，也可以是一门学问。

entries.definition: historical records kept year by year, often official. It is narrower and more institutional than chronology.
entries.definitionCN: 逐年保存的历史记录，常为官方所修。它比 chronology 更窄、更制度化。

entries.definition: a set of things in a fixed order. It need not involve dates and is the broadest term of the group.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定次序排列的一组事物。它不必涉及日期，是这组词中最宽的。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build the word from its Greek halves and then attach it to the places where people actually draw a line of dates.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩用两个希腊半部搭起这个词，再把它系到人们真正画出日期线的地方。

normal.en: Split it: chrono (time) plus logy (study or account). The study of time order, or the account itself.
normal.cn: 拆开：chrono（时间）加 logy（学问或记述）。对时间顺序的研究，或那份记述本身。

normal.en: Picture the police whiteboard: one horizontal line, dates pinned along it.
normal.cn: 想象警方的白板：一条横线，日期钉在上面。

normal.en: Keep the pair relative and absolute chronology: order without numbers, then order with them.
normal.cn: 记住相对年代与绝对年代这一对：先是不带数字的顺序，再是带数字的顺序。

normal.en: See the appendix: biographies end with a bare list of dates.
normal.cn: 看附录：传记末尾是一串纯日期。

normal.en: Watch out for chronicle: it looks like chronology but names a book.
normal.cn: 当心 chronicle：它看起来像 chronology，但指的是一本书。

abstract.en: Hold one line: everything the word does is either drawn on that line or is the craft of drawing it.
abstract.cn: 抓住一条线：这个词所做的一切，要么是画在这条线上，要么是画这条线的手艺。

abstract.en: Sort the senses by scale: a list, a science, a relation, a history, the earth, a life, a case, a story, the universe.
abstract.cn: 按尺度分组：清单、学问、关系、历史、地球、一生、案件、故事、宇宙。

abstract.en: Notice the honesty of the word: a chronology records order and refuses to explain why.
abstract.cn: 留意这个词的诚实：年表只记录先后，拒绝解释原因。

examples.en: The court asked for a detailed chronology of the payments.
examples.cn: 法庭要求提供付款的详细时间线。

examples.en: Radiocarbon dating transformed the chronology of early settlements.
examples.cn: 放射性碳测年改变了早期定居点的年代序列。

examples.en: The book includes a chronology of the author's travels.
examples.cn: 书中附有作者游历的年表。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“克若诺逻辑”：chrono 是时间，logy 是学问——研究时间先后的学问，就是 chronology，年表与年代学。

root: 希腊语 khronos“时间”加 -logia“记述、学问”，16 世纪文艺复兴拉丁语构造为 chronologia；经法语 chronologie 进入英语为 chronology。

sensesIntro.en: Chronology names both the line and the craft of drawing it. Concretely it is a dated list; academically it is the science of establishing dates; abstractly it is the real order of events. It scales from a single night's police timeline to the thirteen-billion-year cosmic one, and at every scale it does the same thing: place events on one axis and let the gaps show.
sensesIntro.cn: chronology 既命名那条线，也命名画线的手艺。具体地说，它是一份带日期的清单；学术地说，它是确定日期的学问；抽象地说，它是事件真实的先后。它可以从一夜的警方时间线扩展到一百三十亿年的宇宙年表，而在每个尺度上它做的都是同一件事：把事件放上一条轴，让空白自己显现。

core.en: One line of dates, and the craft of deciding where each mark belongs.
core.cn: 一条日期线，以及决定每个标记该放哪里的手艺。

branches.en: RECORD: the printed list and the older year-by-year history.
branches.cn: 记录：印出的清单与较早的逐年史书。

branches.en: METHOD AND FACT: the discipline, and the order it tries to recover.
branches.cn: 方法与事实：学问本身，以及它试图复原的先后。

branches.en: DEEP TIME: earth history and cosmic history.
branches.cn: 深时：地球史与宇宙史。

branches.en: SMALL SCALE: one life, one case.
branches.cn: 小尺度：一个人的一生，一个案件。

branches.en: STORY: the order a narrative chooses to use.
branches.cn: 故事：叙述选择使用的顺序。

intro.en: Chronology has two Greek parts and no Latin suffix of its own. The items below follow that build, then add the compound fields that place the word in geology and archaeology, plus the related words for same-time and wrong-time.
intro.cn: chronology 有两个希腊成分，自身不带拉丁后缀。下面的条目沿这个构造展开，再加上把它放进地质学与考古学的复合领域词，以及与“同时”“错时”相关的词。

latinIntro.en: These are Latinised Greek forms, not native Latin. Chronologia is the Renaissance coinage, chronica is the Latin name for a year-by-year record, and chronicus is the Latin adjective from Greek khronikos. They are the channel through which English received the family.
latinIntro.cn: 这些是拉丁化的希腊形式，而非本土拉丁语。chronologia 是文艺复兴造词，chronica 是逐年记录的拉丁名称，chronicus 是希腊 khronikos 的拉丁形容词。英语正是通过这个渠道接收这一词族。

items.meaning: the study of dates; an ordered list of events
items.example: The chronology of the revolt is well documented.
items.exampleCN: 这场起义的经过有详细记载。

items.example: Arrange the photographs in chronological order.
items.exampleCN: 把照片按时间顺序排列。

items.example: The diary entries are printed chronologically.
items.exampleCN: 日记条目按时间顺序印出。

items.meaning: one who studies or fixes dates
items.example: The chronologist disputed the accepted date.
items.exampleCN: 这位年代学家质疑了公认的日期。

items.meaning: the dating of rocks and earth history
items.example: Geochronology relies on radioactive decay.
items.exampleCN: 地质年代学依靠放射性衰变。

items.example: Dendrochronology dated the beam to the fifteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 树木年代学把这根梁断为十五世纪。

items.meaning: a thing out of its proper time
items.example: The clock in the painting is an anachronism.
items.exampleCN: 画中的时钟是时代错置。

items.example: The two revolutions were not synchronous.
items.exampleCN: 这两场革命并非同时发生。

items.meaning: ordering by before and after, without calendar dates
items.example: Relative chronology places the later tomb above the earlier one.
items.exampleCN: 相对年代把较晚的墓排在较早的墓之上。

items.example: Absolute chronology depends on radiocarbon results.
items.exampleCN: 绝对年代依赖碳十四结果。

latinEntries.meaning: the study and ordering of dates

latinEntries.structure: Latin neuter plural of Greek khronika
